tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: Profile of the connected company: name, VAT number, fiscal year start month, base currency, VAT period. Amounts elsewhere are in this currency.

tools.name: list_companies
tools.description: The company this connection is bound to. Always returns exactly ONE company — a token is bound to a single company at grant time and no tool can switch it. Call this first to confirm which entity you are about to write to, and pass the returned id as company_id on write tools to have them refuse if you were wrong.

tools.name: token_info
tools.description: The token this connection uses: the company it is bound to (id and name), how it authenticated (pat or oauth), its scopes, your role in the company, and when it expires. expires_at is the credential on this call; for OAuth the access token renews itself, so reconnect_by (the refresh token's expiry) is when the connector must be re-authorised. Call it before a long run, or when a write is refused for a missing scope.

tools.name: find_by_external_ref
tools.description: Look up IsaFlow records by a source system's own id, e.g. a Sage document id, before creating it again. kind: supplier_invoice, customer_invoice, credit_note, journal, bank_transaction, supplier, customer, or a Sage code (siv, ti, ret, cret, bank, je; ret/cret = supplier/customer credit notes). Returns found: false, or the live match (record) plus any superseded (cancelled, reversed or deleted) rows carrying the same reference. Only records created or imported with external_ref are found; older loads that put the Sage id in a description are not. Needs the read permission of that kind's own list tool (read:invoices, read:reports for journals, read:bank-tx, read:contacts).

id.description: The source system's id for the record

tools.name: trial_balance
tools.description: Trial balance for a fiscal period: EVERY account with its opening balance, the period movement and the closing balance, plus the balanced assertion over exactly the accounts returned. Balance-sheet accounts are cumulative from inception; income-statement accounts are year-to-date within the fiscal year containing the period END, which starts on fiscalYearStart, taken from the fiscal-year registry (the stored year holding the date; every production company here starts in March, not January) — the same figure general_ledger and search_gl close at. openingDebit/openingCredit are the balance at the period start (search_gl's opening). closedToRetainedEarnings is the derived, not posted, year-end close on the account own normal side (search_gl's closedToRetainedEarnings): opening + movement + closedToRetainedEarnings = closing on every row, the derived RE-BF line included (there it is what the closed years added). It is 0 unless the period crosses a fiscal-year start; fiscalYearEndsClosed lists the fiscal-year ends inside the period (empty when none). debitBalance/creditBalance carry the NET closing balance on the account own side, not gross turnover — do not sum them expecting turnover. periodDebit/periodCredit are the turnover. accountCount states how many accounts the balanced assertion covers, and you should check it: a trial balance that omits accounts without movement is a period-movement listing wearing a trial balance name, which is how this report once reported 7 of 118 accounts as Balanced. include_zero_balances separates three states that are NOT the same question. An account is ALWAYS returned when its opening, its closing or its gross movement in the period is non-zero — a balance with no movement, or an income-statement account that opens with a balance and is closed to zero at a fiscal-year start inside the period. An account whose opening, closing and movement are all zero (its postings net to zero before the period) is returned only with the flag on. An account never posted to is never returned. A row with derived:true is computed (the retained-earnings brought-forward line) and has no journal behind it — exclude it when tying this report to the ledger. Paginated: call again with cursor until next_cursor is null. rowsTotal is the full account count, not the size of the page.

fiscal_period_id.description: Fiscal period UUID; defaults to the period containing today.

include_zero_balances.description: Include accounts whose balance AND movement both net to zero. Default false.

tools.name: profit_and_loss
tools.description: Income statement for a date range, LAYERED: turnover, other income, cost of sales, operating expenses, and finance cost / tax reported below the operating line — so operatingProfit means what it says and other income never reaches gross profit. IMPLEMENTATION. This wraps gl/accountClassification#aggregateFigures, the classifier AFS uses. The income-statement PAGE consumes reports/incomeStatementService#getIncomeStatement, and the two now AGREE band for band — turnover, other income, cost of sales, operating expenses, other expenses, gross profit, operating profit and net profit — because both band through the same exported expenseBand/revenueBand and incomeStatementConvergence.test.ts asserts every band. They previously diverged: the page counted other income as turnover and put finance cost and tax inside operating expenses, so it reported a different GROSS profit while the registry claimed the two agreed to the cent (true of net, false of gross). That was finding B75 and it is fixed; do not reconcile a difference that no longer exists. What still differs is scope: this tool has no legacy project_id filter, which the page has. cost_centre_id and business_unit_id RESTRICT every figure, including the comparative and the coverage: cost_centre_id matches a line whose CC1 (cc1_id) or CC2 is that id (the same predicate as the income-statement page and the cc1 grouping), so an FNO filter returns all of its projects and a re-tagged line counts only under its new FNO. Before this the filter reached only the coverage and every band was whole-company. group_by: "cc1" | "cc2" | "bu" adds by_dimension: one column per member (code, name, CC2 parent code, line count and every band) plus an UNTAGGED column for lines with no member, so the columns PARTITION the statement. by_dimension.residual is the ungrouped figure above minus the sum of the columns, per band, to the cent — it must be zero, and ties is the flag. A member id with no master row is its own UNKNOWN column, never merged into untagged. Filters apply before grouping. Unfiltered, the figures above come from a different query, so ties is an independent check; with a filter they come from the same filtered query ungrouped, so ties then proves only that every filtered line landed in exactly one column. classificationCoverage is MANDATORY and present at every detail level, because every band above is chosen from account_subtype and on these books the subtypes barely exist. On one production company 100% of revenue and 97.6% of expenses sit on accounts with no classification, and its classified cost of sales is 2.4% of total costs — so its gross profit is revenue less 2.4% of what it spent. That figure is not a bug; the code did what the chart of accounts told it. READ THE COVERAGE BEFORE ACTING ON ANY BAND. reliable is false when more than 10% of either side is unclassified. Nothing is excluded from any total: an unclassified expense is still an expense, and the classification is the finding rather than a filter. compare: "prior_period" is the preceding whole calendar period (March compares to February, Q2 to Q1), and "prior_year" is the same window one year earlier. Or pass compare_start and compare_end explicitly. This is NOT a rolling window: the page computes its comparative in milliseconds and compares March against 29 January to 28 February, so February never appears as itself.

compare.description: Add a comparative computed on the calendar. Ignored when compare_start/compare_end are given.

cost_centre_id.description: Restrict every figure to one cost centre: lines whose CC1 (cc1_id) or CC2 is this id.

business_unit_id.description: Restrict every figure to one business unit.

group_by.description: Add by_dimension: one column per CC1, CC2 or BU member plus an untagged column, tied to the ungrouped figures.

tools.name: balance_sheet
tools.description: Balance sheet as at a date, with BOTH equity figures rather than the one that always agrees. equityResidual is assets less liabilities and balances by construction — it is not evidence of anything. equityFromLedger is the sum of the POSTED equity-account balances, with nothing derived added to it. Note that totalEquity is NOT the second figure: this report computes retained earnings as revenue less expenses to the date and injects it into the equity section, so totalEquity equals equityResidual by construction and agreeing with it proves nothing. equityDifference is equityResidual − equityFromLedger, and retainedEarningsDerived is the same number named for what it is: profit that no year-end close has posted to an equity account. equityReconciles says whether it is within a cent. On two production companies the equity accounts carry R0.00 and the ENTIRE equity figure is that plug — R8,394,848.60 on one, −R34,816,224.89 on the other. compare_date adds a prior-date column with per-account priorBalance and variance, and BOTH equity figures for the prior date as well. cost_centre_id restricts every figure to one cost centre. equityReconciles is only informative BECAUSE equityFromLedger is now queried from the equity accounts rather than injected. An earlier version compared totalEquity against the residual and returned true on all three production companies — a tautology, since totalEquity equals the residual by construction. Like every self-checking identity here, a true is necessary and not sufficient: two errors that cancel satisfy it, so treat it as a precondition for inspecting the numbers rather than as a conclusion about the books. rows are the account lines of all three sections flattened, each labelled with its section. detail "summary" returns the totals and no rows.

compare_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Adds a prior-date column and its own two equity figures.

cost_centre_id.description: Restrict every figure to one cost centre.

tools.name: aged_debtors
tools.description: Accounts-receivable aging buckets per customer as at a date (defaults to today), WITH the totals. total is the NET over EVERY entity and gross_total is the same figure before credit is netted; buckets (with `disputed`) are gross and over every entity, not just this page — rowsTotal says how many entities there are and truncated says whether you are seeing them all. entity_id drills into one customer or supplier and returns its INVOICES, each with its invoiceNumber, instead of the bucket summary. agedFromInvoiceDate counts invoices with no due date: they ARE in the buckets, aged from their invoice date, so their age is derived rather than known. detail "summary" returns the totals with no rows. Each entity row carries `unapplied` (NEGATIVE — on-account cash plus the face value its live credit notes have not consumed, as at the same date) and `net` = total + unapplied. The BUCKETS plus `buckets.disputed` (AR: open disputes, held outside the five age buckets but still owed) add up to `gross_total`; the headline `total` is the NET, which is what a payment run or a collections call acts on. An entity in credit with no open document still gets a row, with zero buckets and a negative net. The two figures are named separately: the envelope's figureBasis covers the NET total and rows, and gross_figure_basis covers the buckets and gross_total. reconcile_subledger and the REST aging endpoints still report the GROSS figure, so compare like with like. unappliedReceipts and unappliedCreditNotes are the COMPANY-WIDE figures: receipts on the AR control account attached to no invoice, and credit notes with face value left. They are larger than the sum of the rows' `unapplied` by exactly the cash whose customer cannot be resolved, which has no row to sit on. list_unapplied_receipts has the rows and reconcile_subledger explains the gap to the control account. A PAST as_at is reconstructed by unwinding settlement dated since it: payment allocations, credit notes and write-offs. Settlement that left no dated trail — a receipt captured with no allocation row, a migrated balance, a cancelled payment — cannot be unwound, so for those invoices an earlier date reproduces the CURRENT figure rather than what was actually owed then. It will never report an invoice as outstanding once it has been settled.

entity_id.description: Drill into one customer and return its invoices instead of the bucket summary.

tools.name: aged_creditors
tools.description: Accounts-payable aging buckets per supplier as at a date (defaults to today), WITH the totals. total is the NET over EVERY entity and gross_total is the same figure before credit is netted; buckets (with `disputed`) are gross and over every entity, not just this page — rowsTotal says how many entities there are and truncated says whether you are seeing them all. entity_id drills into one customer or supplier and returns its INVOICES, each with its invoiceNumber, instead of the bucket summary. agedFromInvoiceDate counts invoices with no due date: they ARE in the buckets, aged from their invoice date, so their age is derived rather than known. detail "summary" returns the totals with no rows. Each entity row carries `unapplied` (NEGATIVE — on-account cash plus the face value its live credit notes have not consumed, as at the same date) and `net` = total + unapplied. The BUCKETS plus `buckets.disputed` (AR: open disputes, held outside the five age buckets but still owed) add up to `gross_total`; the headline `total` is the NET, which is what a payment run or a collections call acts on. An entity in credit with no open document still gets a row, with zero buckets and a negative net. The two figures are named separately: the envelope's figureBasis covers the NET total and rows, and gross_figure_basis covers the buckets and gross_total. reconcile_subledger and the REST aging endpoints still report the GROSS figure, so compare like with like. unappliedPayments and unappliedCreditNotes are the COMPANY-WIDE figures: payments on the AP control account attached to no bill, and supplier credit notes with face value left. They are larger than the sum of the rows' `unapplied` by exactly the cash whose supplier cannot be resolved, which has no row to sit on. list_unapplied_payments has the rows and reconcile_subledger with subledger "ap" explains the gap to the control account. A PAST as_at is reconstructed by unwinding settlement dated since it: payment allocations, credit notes and write-offs. Settlement that left no dated trail — a receipt captured with no allocation row, a migrated balance, a cancelled payment — cannot be unwound, so for those invoices an earlier date reproduces the CURRENT figure rather than what was actually owed then. It will never report an invoice as outstanding once it has been settled.

entity_id.description: Drill into one supplier and return its invoices instead of the bucket summary.

tools.name: due_by_date
tools.description: What falls due by a date, per customer (receivables) and per supplier (payables), at TODAY's open balances. Per contact: overdueNow (due before today), dueTodayToDate (due today up to and including by_date), totalByDate (their sum: what must be settled by by_date), dueLater (due after by_date), noDueDate (no due date recorded, so it cannot be placed in time). totals are over EVERY contact. overdueNow + dueTodayToDate + dueLater + noDueDate + disputed = total = the aged_debtors / aged_creditors gross total; open customer disputes are held out of the columns (as the aging does) and shown as `disputed`, which `total` includes. netPosition = receivables totalByDate minus payables totalByDate (only when both sides are returned); it LEAVES OUT documents with no due date, whose amounts are in netPositionExcludesNoDueDate. by_date defaults to the end of the current month and must be today or later. side "ar" or "ap" returns one side; omit for both. entity_id (with side) returns that one contact WITH its invoices, each carrying its dueDate (null when none recorded) and bucket; an id with nothing open is an error, not an empty list. Without it contacts carry no invoices.

by_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, today or later; defaults to the end of the current month

side.description: ar = customers, ap = suppliers; omit for both

entity_id.description: One customer or supplier id (needs side): returns that contact with its invoices.

tools.name: reconcile_subledger
tools.description: Reconciles a subledger to its general-ledger control account as at a date, and DECOMPOSES the difference into itemised reconciling items with the ids of the documents behind each one. Use it to answer "why does the AR control account disagree with what customers owe us", not merely "by how much". Returns: subledgerTotal (every open document, including ones that cannot be aged), agedTotal (what aged_debtors/aged_creditors would show), controlAccountBalance, difference, and reconcilingItems. Each item carries a bridge: "aged_to_subledger" items explain why the AGED REPORT total is not the subledger total (open disputes, which aged buckets are net of; unallocated credit notes, which never reach a bucket) and do NOT explain any GL difference; "subledger_to_control" items explain the GL difference itself (unapplied cash, postings no document claims, documents whose value never reached a control account). Those two are separate questions and adding them together produces a number that reconciles to nothing. Each bridge reports its own residual — "unexplained_difference" and "aged_unexplained_difference" — so an incomplete decomposition on either cannot be mistaken for a complete one. controlAccountBalance + the sum of the subledger_to_control items equals subledgerTotal, and agedTotal + the sum of the aged_to_subledger items equals subledgerTotal. POINT IN TIME: as_at moves BOTH sides. The subledger is reconstructed from settlement that can be dated, on the same basis as aged_debtors/aged_creditors — read the limitations on those tools, which apply here unchanged: the reconstruction will not report a settled document as outstanding, but it can UNDERSTATE a past balance where settlement carries no date (bank-match confirmation and the Sage import both write amount_paid with no dated trail). settlementFlagged lists supplier bills whose payment_matched flag says a matching process considered them settled while their balance says nothing was applied — 397 bills worth R16,151,543.00 on one production company. It is an ATTRIBUTION of part of the difference, NOT an extra reconciling item: that cash is already counted once as posting_with_no_document, so its total is deliberately outside reconcilingItems and must not be added to them. WHAT A RESIDUAL OF ZERO DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. READ THIS BEFORE RELYING ON IT. unexplainedDifference of 0.00 is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: it says the items sum to the difference, NOT that they are the right items. Two errors that cancel satisfy it exactly. That is not hypothetical — this endpoint reported 0.00 on every production company while wrongly counting a VAT account as an AP control account, because a reconciling item of the same amount across the same 356 documents removed it again. A phantom control account paired with a phantom offset closes the arithmetic and reads as clean books. Treat zero as a precondition for trusting the decomposition and then INSPECT THE ITEMS: check that controlAccounts holds only accounts you accept as control accounts, and that each item names documents you can follow. A non-zero residual is a mechanism this endpoint does not know about; a zero one is an invitation to look, not a conclusion. CONTROL ACCOUNTS ARE RESOLVED BY SUBTYPE AND BY NOTHING ELSE. There is no canonical control account in this database and no company-level setting names one, so EVERY account carrying the role's subtype (receivable for ar, payable for ap) is returned in controlAccounts and controlAccountAmbiguous is set when more than one does; the balance is their sum. An account is NOT adopted because subledger documents happened to post to it — settle_by_contra posts DR Accounts Payable / CR <loan account> through a supplier payment, and adopting the loan account produced three "AP control accounts", a document_not_on_control_account item of +R453m and an unexplained difference of -R437m, none of it a fact about the books. Accounts a subledger's own documents move in the control direction without carrying the subtype are reported in excludedRows as postings_on_non_control_accounts, with the amount, and the documents whose value went there appear as document_not_on_control_account. Deactivated accounts are included — is_active is a picker flag and says nothing about whether an account holds money. INVARIANTS. The response carries an invariants block, each entry {name, holds, detail}, checked rather than assumed and REPORTED rather than thrown — a violation is the most interesting thing this endpoint can say about a set of books, and a 500 would replace it with nothing. control_plus_items_equals_subledger: controlAccountBalance plus the subledger_to_control items reaches subledgerTotal. item_within_cited_gross: no item claims more than the documents it names are worth, which is what catches an item summed off the wrong column. unexplained_is_the_residual: unexplainedDifference is exactly difference minus the NAMED items, never clamped, floored or plugged. Check holds on all three before reading any figure. UNAPPLIED CASH HAS ONE DEFINITION, shared with list_unapplied_receipts and list_unapplied_payments: a payment's total_amount less its allocations, capped, above a cent. The unapplied_receipt item's AMOUNT is that payment's movement ON THE CONTROL ACCOUNT, because that is what it can explain of the difference, and the item also carries the document figure the listing tools report. Where cash never reached a control account the two differ, and the gap is reported in excludedRows as unapplied_cash_off_control_account rather than folded into an item — on isaflow_dev one company has 130 receipts worth R7.5m in that state against a control balance of -R329,700. posting_with_no_document IS MOSTLY ONE CAUSE CLASS, and it has a remedy: an ALLOCATION JOURNAL WITH NO PAYMENT DOCUMENT. Allocating a bank line posts the control-account journal and, on some paths, creates no supplier_payments or customer_payments row at all — on a production copy 39 journals worth R124,704.80 were in that state, every one of them stamped mcp:bulk_allocate_bank_transactions. Nothing that reads payment rows can see or clear them, so the fix is to create the missing payment document and apply it; list_unapplied_payments and list_unapplied_receipts are blind to them by construction. Reversal journals are NOT in this item: a cancelled payment or credit note nets against its own reversal and both are dropped. settlement_before_document is a document dated AFTER as_at carrying a payment, credit note or write-off posted on or before it — cash applied in advance to a later document (a prepayment); it is timing, not a cut-off error, and is split out of document_not_on_control_account / document_not_linked_to_journal, which now only ever name documents dated on or before as_at. unapplied_credit_note is approved credit no document has consumed. The AP subledger carries no credit notes at all, so supplier credit used to fall into the residual with no name on it; approved credit the AR subledger already counts is deliberately not repeated. Only "ar" and "ap" have a document subledger to compare against; "bank", "vat", "payroll" and "inventory" return the GL control accounts with subledgerTotal null and subledgerUnavailable explaining why, rather than a difference of zero that means nothing. detail: "summary" returns totals only, "standard" (default) returns one row per reconciling item, "full" returns one row per underlying document and is paginated — call again with cursor until next_cursor is null. Follow a documentId with get_invoice, list_invoices or list_journals depending on the item type.

as_at.description: Reporting date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

detail.description: summary = totals only; standard (default) = reconciling items; full = underlying documents.

tools.name: party_ledger_check
tools.description: Statement versus general ledger, PER DOCUMENT, for one supplier or customer. For every document the party has dated on or before as_at -- bills/invoices, credit notes, payments/receipts (contras and refunds are payments with a method), and customer write-offs -- it shows three views side by side: the STATEMENT effect (exactly what supplier_statement / customer_statement counts for it), the SUBLEDGER view (total, settled, and for invoices the outstanding aged_creditors / aged_debtors shows, plus the allocation rows behind the settlement), and the GL view (the net of that document's OWN journal, including any reversals, on the AP/AR control accounts, resolved by subtype exactly as reconcile_subledger does). A document whose statement effect differs from its GL net is flagged with the difference and a reason class. SIGN: every figure points the way the statement does -- positive means the customer owes us / we owe the supplier. REASON CLASSES (statement_vs_gl): document_not_linked_to_journal (an invoice/bill with no journal link), settlement_with_no_journal (a payment, credit note or write-off that reduces the balance but posted nothing), journal_not_posted (linked journal is draft or missing), journal_dated_after_as_at, reversed_journal_live_document (journal reversed while the document is live), excluded_document_has_live_journal (statement leaves it off, e.g. cancelled, but its journal still stands), cancelled_payment_journal_stands (a cancelled payment/receipt whose journal was never reversed: its cash is still on the control account while the statement leaves it off), posted_to_non_control_account (the value went to accounts not typed as the control account; postedTo names them), journal_amount_differs, write_off_not_on_statement (statements do not list write-offs, so the invoice still shows as owed), unclassified_difference (nothing above explains it). SUBLEDGER-TRAIL classes: amount_paid_differs_from_allocations and applied_differs_from_allocations -- the document says it is settled by an amount its allocation rows do not support (a bank-match confirmation writes amount_paid with no allocation row). TOTALS: statementBalance (the statement service), agedNet (the open documents aged_debtors/aged_creditors list for this party, disputes not taken out), glControlNet (sum of the documents' own journals on the control accounts), statementMinusGl, classifiedDifference (what the named classes carry), unexplainedResidual (the rest), and agedBridge, which accounts for agedNet minus statementBalance with unapplied cash, unapplied credit and write-offs. READ THIS BEFORE RELYING ON IT. unexplainedResidual of 0.00 is necessary and NOT sufficient: it says every difference has a name, not that the names are right. Check the invariants block (each {name, holds, detail}); a failing one means a statement line has no document row or the two readers disagree about which documents are open. A bare journal names no party, so journals no document claims cannot be attributed to this party: `unattributed` counts them COMPANY-WIDE and they are outside this party's totals -- if the party has a gap no document explains, look there (reconcile_subledger itemises them). SHARED JOURNALS. One journal can carry several documents (a split bank allocation naming several contacts; a supplier batch posts one journal for all its members). Journal lines name no party, so a document's own leg is counted only when provable: the journal's control lines match its documents' amounts one to one, or the batch total equals the control line. Otherwise the documents get class shared_journal_unattributable, carry no GL view, and are left OUT of statementMinusGl (totals.sharedJournalUnattributable counts them), so the gap is never silently smaller. gl.attribution says which rule applied. COST. Every document of the party is read and compared before detail or limit apply, so summary costs the same as full (a few queries plus one journal-chain walk per document). A party with more than 20,000 documents on or before as_at is refused with the count; use an earlier as_at. detail: "summary" = totals, control accounts, invariants and the party only (small); "standard" (default) = only the FLAGGED documents; "full" = every document, clean ones included. standard and full are paginated: call again with cursor until next_cursor is null. Follow an id with get_invoice, get_supplier_invoice, get_credit_note, list_supplier_payments or list_journals. Read-only; needs read:reports like the statement tools.

party_id.description: Supplier or customer UUID from list_suppliers / list_customers. Required.

detail.description: summary = totals only; standard (default) = flagged documents; full = every document.

tools.name: general_ledger
tools.description: The general ledger for a date range: every posted line, across every account, with a running balance that INCLUDES each account’s opening balance. Use search_gl instead when you want one account and at most 200 rows; use this when you want the whole ledger, several accounts, or a filter. Filters. Account-level (account_codes, account_ids, account_types) select whole accounts and PRESERVE runningBalance. Line-level (sources, min_amount, search) select some of an account’s lines, so runningBalance is null and runningBalanceSuppressed is true — a running total over a subset is not a balance the account ever held. balanced is true only when the period is read UNFILTERED and its debits equal its credits; under any filter it is null, because debits matching credits over a subset is a coincidence and not a check. totalDebit, totalCredit, lineCount and accountCount are over the WHOLE filtered set, never just the page. openingBalances carries an entry for every account in the set, zero included. FISCAL YEAR. Revenue and expense accounts open at the start of the fiscal year containing period_start, not at inception; balance-sheet accounts open cumulatively from inception. If the range crosses a later fiscal-year start, a revenue or expense line dated on or after it has runningBalance null (a cumulative total would not be the trial balance’s, and no year-end line is inserted here), and incomeStatementBalanceNullFrom names that start date; it is null when the range crosses none. Balance-sheet lines are never nulled. search_gl, for one account, inserts derived year-end close rows and keeps the balance. RE-BF: an UNFILTERED read adds an openingBalances key RE-BF, the retained earnings brought forward — the profit earned before that fiscal-year start, credit positive (negative is an accumulated loss), omitted when under 1 cent. It is derived, not a posted account: it has no lines and is not counted in accountCount. A filtered read never carries it. Paging: call again with cursor set and every other argument unchanged until next_cursor is null. Every line is served exactly once. COMPLETENESS: universeTotal is the UNFILTERED posted line count for the period, so rowsTotal below it means you are holding an extract and excludedTotal says how many lines your filters removed. An unfiltered call has excludedTotal 0 and rowsTotal equal to universeTotal. universeTotal is the window's own count even when your filters match nothing (rowsTotal 0, excludedTotal equal to universeTotal); it is 0 only when the window genuinely holds no posted line. search is a case-insensitive LITERAL substring of the entry number or description (% and _ are not wildcards). detail: "summary" returns totals only; "standard" (default) and "full" return lines. group_by=account|month|source|account_type adds groups (line_count, total_debit, total_credit per group, over the same filtered lines as the totals; they sum to the totals; at most 200 groups, the rest summed in other) to the summary and implies detail "summary"; it takes no cursor. A page of 1000 lines passes 90 KB: use the grouped summary first, then page only the account you need.

account_codes.description: Restrict to these account codes. Preserves runningBalance.

account_ids.description: Restrict to these account UUIDs. Preserves runningBalance.

account_types.description: Restrict to these account types. Preserves runningBalance.

sources.description: Journal sources (e.g. manual, auto_invoice). SUPPRESSES runningBalance.

min_amount.description: Only lines whose debit or credit is at least this. SUPPRESSES runningBalance.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of the entry number or description. SUPPRESSES runningBalance.

group_by.description: Group the summary by one of: account, month, source, account_type. Implies detail "summary".

tools.name: search_gl
tools.description: General-ledger lines for one account over a date range, with running balance. Provide account_id or account_code plus from_date/to_date. Max 200 rows. Balances are exact to the cent. A revenue or expense account opens at the start of the fiscal year containing from_date, and when the range crosses a later fiscal-year start the rows include a derived year-end close row at each boundary where the balance is not zero: source "year_end_close", derived true, empty journalEntryId, description "Closed to retained earnings — FY ending <date> (derived — not posted)". It zeroes the running balance, so the closing balance equals the trial balance as at to_date. Close rows count toward total and the row limit. closedToRetainedEarnings is the normal-side total of those close rows, negated (0 when none, and always 0 for a balance-sheet account); periodClosingBalance = openingBalance + periodNet + closedToRetainedEarnings.

tools.name: list_gl_accounts
tools.description: The company's chart of accounts — resolve account codes to UUIDs in one call before allocate/journal tools, instead of one search_gl per code. Optionally filter by account_type or by a case-insensitive substring of the code or name. Returns at most 250 rows per call (default 200), ordered by account_code. Paging: the reply carries next_cursor whenever more rows match; call again with cursor set and every other argument unchanged until next_cursor is null. total is the full match count.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of account_code or account_name

active_only.description: Exclude deactivated accounts. Defaults to true.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: Customer invoices, newest first. Filter by status (draft/sent/paid/…), customer_id, or free-text search. Returns {invoices, total, next_offset}: up to `limit` rows (default 25, max 100); when next_offset is not null, call again with offset=next_offset for the next page. To total a large book without paging, use detail="summary" (count, total_amount, amount_paid and balance over the WHOLE filter set, no rows) and group_by=customer|status|month (groups sum to the totals; at most 200 groups, the rest summed in other). A summary takes no offset.

status.description: Invoice status, or omit for all

search.description: Matches invoice number or customer name

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

detail.description: summary = totals (and groups, with group_by) over the whole filter set, no rows. Default standard (rows).

group_by.description: Group the summary by one of: customer, status, month. Implies detail "summary".

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description: One customer invoice by id, including line items.

tools.name: list_quotes
tools.description: Customer quotes, newest first. Filter by status or search. Max 100 rows.

tools.name: list_customers
tools.description: Customers of the connected company (name, contact details, payment terms, VAT number, default_revenue_account_id), ordered by name. Optional free-text search. Returns {customers, next_offset}: up to `limit` rows (default 100, max 150); when next_offset is not null, call again with offset=next_offset for the next page (null means that was the last page).

search.description: Matches name, email, VAT number, or contact person

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

tools.name: list_suppliers
tools.description: Suppliers of the connected company (name, company, contact details, payment terms), ordered by name. Optional search. Returns {suppliers, total, next_offset}: up to `limit` rows (default 25, max 200); when next_offset is not null, call again with offset=next_offset for the next page.

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

tools.name: bank_accounts_status
tools.description: Bank accounts with balances, allocation counts and unreconciledCount (posted lines neither reconciled nor excluded). reconciledBalance / unreconciledBalance are JOURNAL-based despite their names: the net of lines with / without a journal line (unreconciledBalance excludes excluded lines), not reconciliation state. Includes inactive (deactivated) accounts: this is a question about money, and an inactive account still holds a balance and an unreconciled backlog. Each row carries isActive — false means the account is no longer offered when coding new transactions, so report its balance but never pick it as the target of a new allocation or payment.

tools.name: list_bank_transactions
tools.description: Bank transactions, filterable by account, allocation state, and date range. limit is capped at 100 rows per call: a larger value is ACCEPTED and silently clamped to 100, so page with cursor rather than raising limit. allocation_filter: allocated = a journal books the line (a posted journal line, or a provisional / reconciled line); suggested = categorised/AI-suggested but not yet posted; unallocated = neither. An excluded line is in none of them, even if it kept a journal match. Paging: the reply carries next_cursor whenever more rows match. To read a whole account, call again with cursor set to that value and every other argument unchanged, and keep looping until next_cursor is null. fields="compact" returns only id, date, amount, bank_reference and allocation (~10x smaller) — use it when you are scanning or bulk-allocating and do not need the full row. compact bank_reference is the statement reference from either column (the row's bank_reference, else its reference), which is exactly what allocate_bank_transaction and bulk_allocate_bank_transactions resolve. compact allocation is one of allocated | suggested | unallocated | excluded | pending; an excluded row is returned by NO allocation_filter, so never treat one as work to do, and pending means the line is still pending at the bank (not yet posted; no allocation_filter returns it and it cannot be allocated until it posts). description_contains: case-insensitive substring matched against the statement description OR reference (a literal match — % and _ are not wildcards). It combines with every other filter (bank_account_id, allocation_filter, dates) and with cursor paging, and total counts only the matching lines. A full row is 0.5 to 1 KB, so a 100-row page can approach or pass 90 KB: to size or total a large window, use detail="summary" (counts and money in/out/net over the WHOLE filter set, no rows) and group_by=account|month|allocation (groups sum to the totals; allocation is allocated|suggested|unallocated|excluded|pending). A summary takes no cursor.

description_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the description or reference.

detail.description: summary = totals (and groups, with group_by) over the whole filter set, no rows. Default standard (rows).

group_by.description: Group the summary by one of: account, month, allocation. Implies detail "summary".

tools.name: get_match_candidates
tools.description: Scored match candidates for a single bank transaction (supplier invoices, customer invoices, purchase orders, journal lines). Read-only. Use before allocate_bank_transaction to decide what a line belongs to.

tools.name: vat_status
tools.description: The VAT201 for a period, computed live from posted journals. Give the VAT period start and end dates (YYYY-MM-DD; South African VAT periods are normally two calendar months). Returns the SARS boxes, each with BOTH the value of the supply (base) and the tax posted against it, plus totals: box 4 output tax, box 19 input tax, box 20 net VAT payable (positive) or refundable (negative). rateCheck runs SARS's own 15% test before you file: impliedTax is base x 15% and variance is tax minus that. ties=false means the ledger disagrees with itself and the return will be queried — read the per-box variance to find which box, then detail="full" for the journals behind it. rateCheck.inputVariance is NOT the box total: it is the input tax OVER-claimed, summed journal by journal (an under-claim on one bill cannot hide an over-claim on another), so it can be non-zero while every input box variance reads 0. detail: "summary" = boxes and totals only, no transactions; "standard" (the default, also spelled "boxes") = boxes plus the VAT journal lines, paged; "full" = the same lines each with the base legs of their journal, which is what shows you WHAT was supplied or purchased. Page with cursor until next_cursor is null. excludedRows carries VAT the report could not place in any box — most often tax posted to an account with no VAT posting treatment, which is money SARS is owed or owed to you that no box reports. Read it: it is not a footnote. LIMITS: posted journals only, so drafts are invisible; the period is taken literally from entry_date, so a journal dated outside its VAT period lands in the wrong return; and this computes the return, it does not file it.

tools.name: vat_reconciliation
tools.description: Reconciles VAT month by month across three sources: what the general ledger posted, what the invoices say, and what was actually submitted on a VAT return. Returns each month with GL revenue and VAT, invoice revenue and VAT, the submitted return where one exists, the capital-goods split, the variance between each pair, and the effective VAT rate. issues[] flags a month whose effective rate falls outside 14–16% (a misclassification of zero-rated or exempt supplies), a revenue or output-VAT variance above the threshold, and any month with no return submitted at all. USE IT FOR: "does the VAT control account agree with what we filed", and "how much VAT is sitting in the ledger that SARS has never been told about" — R1,383,192 of apparent shortfall on one company was assembled by hand from a bank export before this existed. LIMITS: a month with no vat_returns record shows returnOutputVat null and a variance of 0, which means NOT SUBMITTED, not "agrees". Supplier-invoice input VAT is not carried in the invoice column (invoiceInputVat is always 0) — compare glInputVat instead. It reports; it files nothing.

tools.name: vat201_export
tools.description: The VAT201 in a form you can file: the SARS field codes (F01–F16) with their values, or a CSV of the boxes. Computed from the SAME journal-derived boxes as vat_status, so the return you export is the one the 15% check was run against. format: "sars_payload" (the default) returns the field codes; "csv" returns a spreadsheet of every box with its base, tax, implied tax at 15% and variance, and the VAT the boxes could not place. rateCheck is carried through: DO NOT FILE a return whose ties is false without reading the per-box variance first — that is the check SARS runs. If the period has been locked by lock_vat_period, the lock is returned, and driftSinceLock is non-null when the ledger no longer computes what was filed. That is evidence that something was posted into a filed period, not an updated return. blockingExceptions carries getVatExceptions' blocking counts as a WARNING ONLY — this tool never refuses on them, unlike lock_vat_period and manual mark-submitted. LIMITS: it produces the payload; it does not submit anything to SARS and does not create a vat_returns record.

tools.name: vat_exceptions
tools.description: The pre-filing VAT exceptions for a period — every type, each marked blocking or non-blocking, with its count and its items (journal ids/numbers, invoice numbers, amounts). BLOCKING types (refuse lock_vat_period and manual mark-submitted unless an owner/admin overrides with a reason; ALWAYS refuse SARS ISV filing, no override): uncodedGlLines, invoiceTaxCodeIssues (CUSTOMER invoices only, Hein 2026-09-27 — can only mean under-declared output VAT), invoiceGlMismatches, vatOnBalanceSheetLines, vatNonSupplyLines, controlRecon (its own reconExceptions, from output/input variance), unpostedInvoiceVat (also journal_dated_after_period, Hein 2026-09-27 — a CUSTOMER invoice's journal posted with an entry_date AFTER the invoice's own period end; time of supply is the invoice date, so its output VAT is missing from this period even though the journal did eventually post. SUPPLIER bills never carry this reason: a later journal date there is a legitimate late input-VAT claim under s16(3)), and unsupportedInputVat (input VAT that DISAGREES with what supports it — amount_mismatch or document_over_claimed, the return's figures would be wrong — or document_unlinked, Hein 2026-09-26: a document WAS linked, evidencing the claim, and no longer is, with nothing else supporting it). NON-BLOCKING (informational — visible, never hidden): billTaxCodeWarnings (Hein, 2026-09-27 — SUPPLIER bills with no tax rate, or a rate but zero VAT: can only mean LESS input VAT was claimed than the bill's own rate supports, never more, with potentialInputVat = subtotal * taxRate/100 per row; if the supplier is a VAT vendor the input VAT can still be claimed as a late claim, otherwise the rate should be corrected to zero/exempt), declaredElsewhereVat (marked "VAT declared outside IsaFlow", mark_vat_declared_elsewhere) and inputVatWithoutTaxInvoice — a claim supported only by a bank line or a VAT adjustment ("no tax invoice on file"), or with no document link at all or an unreadable document VAT (Hein, 2026-09-26 — a RECORD is missing, not a wrong figure; holding the tax invoice is the vendor's legal responsibility and it may live outside IsaFlow, so these no longer block). totalExceptions is the SAME number lock_vat_period and eFiling check. overrideHistory lists every recorded override for this exact period (vat_gate_overrides), newest first — who overrode what, when, and the exception counts at the time. controlRecon ties the FILED ledger VAT201 (fields 5/10) to the GL VAT control account movement; its own output/input variance is what reconExceptions counts. degradedData true means a source query failed and every total here is UNDER-counted — do not treat this as clean.

tools.name: document_vat_history
tools.description: EVERY VAT LINE TIED TO ONE DOCUMENT, AND THE VAT IT CARRIES NOW. entity_type supplier_invoice, customer_invoice or credit_note; entity_id from list_supplier_invoices / list_invoices / list_credit_notes. One row per VAT line (journal id, number, date, source, status, reversed, GL account, vat_type, vat_amount signed in the document's own direction — positive = the way its posting moved VAT — and net_base where derivable) with tie: posting (its own journal), late_claim (its s16(3) late-claim companion), reversal (the posting's reversal chain), credit_note (a LINKED note's journal and its cancel), and the HEURISTIC reference_match / narration_match: a posted journal of any source that is not the posting of an invoice, bill or credit note (hand journals, bank allocations — a supplier refund posts as a supplier payment —, imports, write-offs; another document's posting that names the number matches too), dated in or after the document's fiscal period, with a line on one of its own VAT accounts, whose reference or narration names its number as a whole token; only its lines on those accounts count. Totals: vat_posted, vat_derivable_now (what the posting, companion, reversals and credit notes leave), vat_heuristic, vat_heuristic_reducing, vat_net_now (derivable plus each match's NEGATIVE net — a match that adds VAT never offsets one that took it away), vat_reversed, vat_by_tie, net_base_posted, net_base_now; heuristic.matches lists each match with its chain's net. heuristic.searched says whether a search ran; notes explains gaps (a cancelled document no longer names its posting). Check heuristic matches before relying on them. Only posted journals count, as the VAT201 reads them, future-dated ones included. Use before crediting a bill (create_credit_note mirror_bill reads the same figures) to avoid reversing its VAT twice.

tools.name: data_integrity_checks
tools.description: Runs a suite of sixteen integrity checks over the ledger and returns, for each, how many rows fail it, the money behind them, and a sample you can go and open. Checks: invoices_null_due_date (invisible in the aging) · vat_displayed_differs_from_posted (the bank screen shows no VAT and the journal claims it) · journal_date_differs_from_bank_date (a day decides the VAT period) · duplicate_bank_references (the reference is not a key) · deactivated_accounts_with_balance · asset_accounts_with_credit_balance · cost_of_sales_typed_as_expense (gross profit) · clearing_accounts_not_nil · duplicate_control_accounts (two accounts receiving one role) · documents_outside_open_period · stale_suggested_transactions (look done, not in the GL) · test_records_in_production · invoices_without_revenue_line · payment_matched_but_unapplied (flagged as paid with the balance still open) · project_fno_mismatch (a journal or bank line whose stored FNO/CC1 is not the one its project/CC2 derives through the current parent chain) · paye_payable_differs_from_emp201 (a month's PAYE payable on 2140 from payroll journals differs from the EMP201's, ETI carry included). Pass checks:[...] to run a subset; omit it to run all sixteen. as_at scopes every check to a reporting date and defaults to today. limit caps the SAMPLE only — count and amount are always over every failing row, so count > sample.length simply means there are more. READ THIS BEFORE ACTING ON A ZERO: a check whose query failed comes back with count -1 and appears in excludedRows. That is "unknown", not "clean", and it is the one result you must never treat as a pass. LIMITS: this reports, it never fixes anything and never changes a row. Two checks (clearing_accounts_not_nil, cost_of_sales_typed_as_expense) match on the account NAME, because no subtype records the intent — they compare the name against the type rather than computing from it, so a differently-named clearing account is not found.

checks.description: Subset to run. Omit for all sixteen.

limit.description: Sample rows per check. Never caps count or amount.

tools.name: chart_of_accounts_health
tools.description: Audits the chart of accounts itself: accounts with no subtype, subtypes that do not belong to their account type, accounts never posted to, deactivated accounts still carrying a balance, duplicated codes, two accounts that are the same account under different codes, and whether an imported chart and the system chart are running on top of each other. Returns a summary with a count per finding, the flagged accounts (worst first, then largest balance), and systemRoles — every one of the fifteen system account roles, with the ones the ledger cannot resolve broken out in missingSystemAccounts, each carrying how it is empty and which accounts nearly claim it. READ THE GAP, NOT JUST THE ROLE NAME. An empty role reports HOW it is empty, because the fix differs: no_claimant means no account carries the subtype and one must be created; unflagged_active_claimant means an active account already carries it and is merely missing is_system_account (creating a second account here makes the chart worse — one company had 8,342 bank transactions on an unflagged account beside two empty deactivated ones); deactivated_claimants_only means the right account exists and needs reactivating. Each empty role lists the candidate accounts already in the chart. contestedSystemAccounts is the opposite failure: more than one active system account claims one role, so the resolver picks deterministically between them and every auto-posting depends on that pick. WHY IT MATTERS: none of this unbalances a trial balance, which is why it survives. An account with no subtype is invisible to the income statement bucketing, the VAT201 and the system account resolver, and lands in whatever the default happens to be — that is how R81m of cost of sales was reported as operating expenses. LIMITS: it reports and changes nothing. overlaidCharts is only as good as the imported_from column: a chart imported before that column was populated reads as a single chart, so treat false as "not detected" rather than "not happening". Duplicate NAMES are matched after collapsing case and punctuation; two accounts that are the same account under different names are not found. The role check reads the subtype column only: an account that SHOULD hold a role but carries a different subtype (or none) reads as no_claimant, because nothing in the schema records the intent.

tools.name: list_agent_postings
tools.description: SUPERSEDED BY audit_trail — prefer that unless you are already paginating against this one. This tool can only see postings that are ALREADY provable (posting_agent LIKE 'mcp:%'), so it is blind to agent work that was written without the stamp; audit_trail reports every posting with its actor and whether that actor was recorded or inferred. GL journal entries created by an MCP tool for this company, selected by ENTRY DATE (not by when the tool ran), with the tool that made each one. Covers every MCP connection on the company, not only this one, and includes entries that are still DRAFT (create_draft_journal) alongside posted ones — read the status field. Use to review what the agent did before accepting or reversing it. Each row carries reversed: true once a contra has been posted against it — status stays "posted" after a reversal, so reversed is the only signal that a posting has already been corrected; do not reverse those again. reversalOfId is set when the row is itself a reversal contra. Returns at most `limit` rows (default 50, max 100), newest entry date first — a range with more entries than that is truncated, not summarised.

tools.name: audit_trail
tools.description: WHO POSTED TO THE GENERAL LEDGER, and whether that attribution is a recorded fact or an inference. One row per GL journal entry in an entry-date range, with the actor (human | agent | system), the MCP token behind an agent posting, the posting_agent stamp, and the entry's status and amount. TWO PEOPLE, NOT ONE: user_id/user_name is who RAISED the entry, posted_by_user_id/posted_by_user_name is who COMMITTED it to the ledger. Across every production company today those are the SAME person on every single journal — there is no segregation of duties anywhere in this system, and that is a control conclusion you can state from this endpoint in one line rather than sampling for it. A draft has no poster at all. company_id, on the response rather than on each row, is whose books these are — the token decides it, so a page is never mixed. WHICH FIRM the actor was acting for is acting_company_id — the practice, on a client engagement. Read acting_company_known first: when it is false the firm was NOT RECORDED, and cross_company is null, meaning UNKNOWN. Null is not "in-house": it is the absence of a record, and every row written before migration 581 has it. Never read a null as "posted from inside this company". Filter posted_from_outside_this_company to get only postings made into these books by someone acting for a DIFFERENT recorded company — the first question a client's auditor asks of a practice engagement. Rows with no recorded firm can never satisfy it, so that filter under-reports while the write side is still being built. READ actor_provenance ON EVERY ROW. "recorded" means the write itself stored the actor. "derived" means it was inferred from the posting_agent stamp because the row predates that column, and the inference is ASYMMETRIC: an "mcp:" stamp does prove an agent, but a "human:" one proves only "not stamped as an agent" — journal creation falls back to a human stamp whenever a caller omits the posting metadata, so an unknown number of agent postings sit under derived human. actor_caveat spells this out per row. Never report a derived human as a person having typed the entry. AND A RECORDED HUMAN IS A WEAKER CLAIM THAN IT LOOKS: nothing in IsaFlow writes actor_type "human" by default, so a recorded human means some caller explicitly asserted one — it is not produced by a person using the UI, and the absence of an agent stamp is not proof of a person. An agent posting is provable; a human posting is not. Say "not recorded as an agent", never "typed by a person". The attribution block totals recorded vs derived across the whole filtered range (not just the page), which is the honest measure of how much of this ledger can be relied on. DOES NOT COVER: non-ledger changes. Editing a customer, changing a bank rule or logging in leaves no journal and does not appear here; entity_history has who changed which supplier, customer, GL / bank account, employee, member or company setting, and from what to what. Nor does it cover documents that have not posted — an unapproved draft invoice or credit note has no journal yet. entity_id needs an entity_type saying which link to match: "journal" = the entry's own id, "source_record" = the bank transaction / invoice / credit note it was raised from, "source_document" = the captured document. universeTotal is present unless an actor_type, token_jti or acting_company_id filter is applied — with one the result is a selection, not a census, and completeness is not a claim being made. Rows whose actor cannot be established at all (neither column set) are never counted in the totals; they appear in excludedRows with reason "unattributed_posting", and excludedTotal counts ALL of them while excludedRows shows at most 200 — truncatedExcludedRows tells you when the list is shorter than the count. Paginate with next_cursor; at most 200 rows per page. Free to call — reviewing what was posted is the control every write depends on.

actor_type.description: Matches recorded actors AND the equivalent legacy posting_agent stamp.

token_jti.description: Only postings made by one MCP token — the first question after a credential is withdrawn. Recorded postings only.

acting_company_id.description: Only postings made while acting for this firm. Recorded firms only; rows with no recorded firm never match.

posted_from_outside_this_company.description: Only postings whose recorded acting company DIFFERS from the company whose books these are. Rows with no recorded firm are excluded — they cannot answer the question either way.

user_id.description: The user the entry is booked against (created_by).

source.description: Journal source, e.g. manual, auto_bank_recon, auto_invoice.

action.description: Derived from the entry: reversed beats posted beats draft.

detail.description: summary returns totals and the attribution census with no rows.

tools.name: entity_history
tools.description: WHO CHANGED A SUPPLIER, CUSTOMER, GL / BANK ACCOUNT, EMPLOYEE, EMPLOYEE BANK DETAILS, MEMBER OR COMPANY SETTING, AND FROM WHAT TO WHAT. One row per write that changed a master-data record, recorded by the database itself whoever wrote it (the app, an MCP token, Login-as, the platform admin portal, a script, raw SQL), newest first: op (create / update / delete), the changed fields with their before and after values, the actor (a user id, or db:<role> for a write with no signed-in user) and the channel — session (a person signed in as themselves), impersonation (Login-as; impersonator is the platform admin behind it), token (an API / MCP token), platform_admin, system. Bank account numbers and ID / tax numbers are MASKED to their last four characters (masked: true); employee bank details also mask the branch code to its last two digits and the account holder to its first letter. Employee bank-detail history is returned masked to a token holder with owner / admin / manager and read:payroll by design (Hein, 2026-11-04). A changed value still shows as changed. Netcash keys are recorded only as a sha256 digest. entity_id needs entity_type. Without entity_id this is the company-wide feed (optionally one entity_type), owner / admin only. Members, invitations, permissions, company settings, approval rules and switches: owner / admin; employees and their bank details: owner / admin / manager with the read:payroll scope; suppliers and customers need read:contacts (the feed leaves out any type a scope is missing for). History starts when migration 888 was deployed; earlier changes were not recorded. Bank rules have their own history (list_bank_rules). Paginate with next_cursor; at most 100 rows per page.

entity_id.description: Requires entity_type. E.g. a supplier id from list_suppliers.

tools.name: audit_snapshots
tools.description: SEALED AUDIT SNAPSHOTS OF THE BOOKS. Without snapshot_id: the company's snapshots, newest first — cutoff, when and by whom taken, trigger (manual / period_close / vat_lock / year_close), status (sealed, or failed with the reason), canonical hash; status unchanged = the books (ledger, ageing and control totals) read the same as an earlier sealed snapshot (same_as_snapshot_id), with its own sealed check run. verify_chain: true checks the company's chain of sealed snapshots for a missing or replaced link, and lists sealed rows whose seal does not verify (forged) separately. With snapshot_id: that snapshot's header and totals plus its check run (15 integrity checks, the anomaly scan and the journal-risk leads, each with status pass / fail / unknown and its findings). With verify: true: recompute every row hash and the canonical hash from what is stored and check the HMAC seal — status valid, invalid (a row, hash or seal does not match, or the seal names a key the server does not hold), not_sealed or unchanged. A snapshot holds the current values of records dated on or before its cutoff, as at taken_at — not the historical database state. Owner, admin or manager.

verify.description: With snapshot_id: verify the seal from the stored rows.

verify_chain.description: Without snapshot_id: check the company's chain of sealed snapshots (broken links, forged rows).

tools.name: compare_audit_snapshot
tools.description: WHAT CHANGED IN THE BOOKS BEHIND A SNAPSHOT. Compares a sealed snapshot with today's books at its cutoff (or, with against_snapshot_id, with a later snapshot at the same or a later cutoff): journals dated on or before the cutoff that are new — backdated ones (created or posted after the snapshot was taken) listed with who and when — changed ones with field-level before / after and their line changes, removed ones with their status now, ones reversed after the snapshot, the closing balance of every account that moved, and (against today) master-data changes recorded since the snapshot. Read-only. A snapshot holds the current values of records dated on or before its cutoff, as at taken_at — not the historical database state. Owner, admin or manager.

against_snapshot_id.description: Optional: a later snapshot instead of today's books.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: Supporting documents on file. THERE ARE TWO SEPARATE STORES and this reads whichever one you address. Give from and to (and optionally bank_transaction_id) to list the receipts, slips and invoice scans attached to BANK TRANSACTIONS — the read side of attach_document (needs read:bank-tx as well as read:reports). Those rows carry store "bank_attachment" (an uploaded file) or "captured_document" (a captured document linked to the bank line that has no uploaded copy, e.g. one over 2 MB); both count as the line's supporting documents. Give entity_type and entity_id instead to list the documents filed against one accounting document (supplier_invoice, supplier_payment, customer_invoice, customer_payment, credit_note, bank_transaction), including documents cross-linked from another entity, which come back with source "linked" and a link_reason. entity_type bank_transaction with the line's id lists that one line's documents from the bank store (rows as above, no date range needed; needs read:bank-tx as well), so a caller never has to know which store holds what. DOES NOT COVER: a company-wide listing of the entity store. Those rows carry no company id and are fenced by their parent document, so they can only be read one entity at a time — there is no "all documents for this company" query, and asking for one would silently cross tenants. Nor does it return file bytes; use get_document for a single file. To find what has NO document, use list_unsupported_transactions — an empty page here means nothing was found for what you asked, not that nothing exists. Paging: up to limit documents per call (default 50, max 75); the reply carries next_offset, null on the last page, else call again with offset=next_offset. The entity store pages its direct and cross-linked documents side by side, so a page can hold up to twice the limit. To size the bank store without paging, use detail="summary" (count and file_size in bytes over the WHOLE from/to window, no rows) and group_by=store|month (groups sum to the totals). A summary takes no offset and is for the bank store only; one entity's documents are listed directly.

from.description: Transaction date from, YYYY-MM-DD. Bank store only.

to.description: Transaction date to, YYYY-MM-DD. Bank store only.

bank_transaction_id.description: Narrows the bank store to one transaction.

entity_id.description: With entity_type, reads the entity store instead.

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

detail.description: summary = totals (and groups, with group_by) over the whole filter set, no rows. Default standard (rows).

group_by.description: Group the summary by one of: store, month. Implies detail "summary".

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: One bank-transaction document by id (store "bank_attachment" or "captured_document" from list_documents), with its file name, size, mime type and the transaction it supports. A captured document's content is returned only up to 4 MB; past that content_omitted says "too_large". Set include_content to also get the file as base64 — omit it unless you will actually read the bytes, since a scan can be several hundred kilobytes of response. DOES NOT COVER the entity document store (documents filed against an invoice or credit note): those are held in external file storage rather than inline, so list_documents returns their metadata and they must be fetched through the application.

include_content.description: Return the file bytes as base64. Default false.

tools.name: list_unsupported_transactions
tools.description: Bank transactions with NO supporting document attached — the "which transactions over R10,000 have no receipt" audit test. min_amount is compared against the ABSOLUTE amount, so a R12,000 payment out is caught as readily as one in. Rows come back largest first. transactions_in_scope is every transaction in the range over the threshold; transactions_with_a_document is how many of those do have one, so the two figures size the exposure rather than merely listing it. LIMIT: "supporting document" here means a document on the BANK TRANSACTION itself: a file attached to it (attach_document) or a captured document linked to it. A transaction whose evidence was filed against the related invoice instead is still reported as unsupported — those two stores are not linked. Treat the result as a list to check, not a list of failures.

min_amount.description: Materiality threshold on ABS(amount). Default 0 — everything.

tools.name: list_missing_documents
tools.description: Accounting documents with NO supporting document on file: supplier bills, customer invoices, credit notes, bank SPEND lines and journals that claim input VAT. The audit test "what is undocumented?" in one call, largest first. Whether a document exists is computed from the document tables on every call, never read from a cached flag, and uses the same tests as the bill has_document flag, the bills "Missing document" filter, list_unsupported_transactions and the pre-filing VAT input warnings, so they agree. entity_types (default: every type this token may read): supplier_invoice, customer_invoice, credit_note, bank_transaction, vat_journal. Reading bills, invoices and credit notes needs read:invoices, bank lines read:bank-tx, VAT journals read:vat; types the token lacks the scope for come back in skipped_entity_types. from / to bound the document date (YYYY-MM-DD) and may span at most 24 months; default is the last 12 months to today, echoed back. min_amount is a materiality threshold on the absolute amount (default 0). A customer invoice counts as documented through the app's own PDF snapshot of the invoice it issued (its source document) as well as an uploaded file; a bill needs an uploaded file or a stored source scan, and a link to the bill's purchase order or goods receipt paperwork does not count. amount is the gross total for bills, invoices and credit notes, the absolute amount for a bank line, and the input VAT claimed for a vat_journal. summary gives, per type, candidates (rows checked), with_document, missing and missing_amount over the WHOLE range, not just the page; vat_journal has no candidates count because the VAT check reports only its exceptions. Draft and cancelled bills, invoices and credit notes are not checked; bank lines that are not spend, are excluded, or are own-account transfers are not either. A bank line whose receipt was filed against the related bill is still reported on the line (the two stores are not linked), and a VAT journal built from an undocumented bank line is reported under both types, so the per-type figures overlap and are not summed. detail "summary" returns the summary only. Rows are paged with next_cursor (at most 200 per page). Each row names the tool that files the missing document.

from.description: Document date from, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: 12 months before to.

to.description: Document date to, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today.

min_amount.description: Materiality threshold on the absolute amount. Default 0.

tools.name: list_proofs_of_payment
tools.description: Every ABSA proof of payment (POP) filed from the company's mirrored mailbox, newest payment first, with what became of it. match.status: attached (the matcher attached the POP to its bank line, bank_transaction_id), attached_manually (the matcher did not, whatever it decided, but a person linked the POP's document to a bank line in the app: bank_transaction_id; nothing to do), ambiguous (several lines, or another POP, matched: nothing attached; candidate_bank_transaction_ids is the suggestion for a person), not_found (no single free line yet; re-checked until payment_date + 45 days), refused (one line matched but the attach was refused: refusal), pending (not looked at yet). archive.status: archived (copied to SharePoint: web_url, path), too_large (over 4 MB, never uploaded), failed (gave up after repeated failures: last_error), pending (not copied yet; attempts / tries / last_error when it has failed before). archive_configured false means the company has no SharePoint target, so every POP stays archive pending. Filters: match_status (a status above, or unmatched = every POP on no bank line: neither attached nor attached_manually), archive_status, date_from / date_to on the payment date (YYYY-MM-DD), beneficiary (case-insensitive substring, literal). total and summary (counts by match status and by archive status) are over the WHOLE filter, not just the page. Up to limit rows (default 50, max 50); call again with offset=next_offset until it is null. Read-only.

date_from.description: Payment date on or after, YYYY-MM-DD

date_to.description: Payment date on or before, YYYY-MM-DD

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

tools.name: list_supplier_invoices
tools.description: List supplier invoices (accounts payable / bills). Filter by status, supplier_id, date range, or a free-text search over invoice number, supplier name and reference. Returns {invoices, total, offset} — total is the pre-limit match count, so a truncated page is visible rather than assumed complete. Page with offset. A page of 200 can pass 90 KB: to total a large book use detail="summary" (count, total_amount, amount_paid and balance over the WHOLE filter set, no rows) and group_by=supplier|status|month (groups sum to the totals; at most 200 groups, the rest summed in other). A summary takes no offset.

search.description: Free text over invoice number, supplier name and reference

detail.description: summary = totals (and groups, with group_by) over the whole filter set, no rows. Default standard (rows).

group_by.description: Group the summary by one of: supplier, status, month. Implies detail "summary".

tools.name: get_supplier_invoice
tools.description: Fetch one supplier invoice by id, including its line items and the gl_account_id each line posts to (resolve codes with list_gl_accounts).

tools.name: list_bank_rules
tools.description: List the bank categorisation rules for this company. Rules match incoming bank transactions and, when auto_create_entry is true, POST a journal automatically — so read this BEFORE importing a statement or retiring an account, otherwise a stale rule will silently re-route transactions to the old account. Returns the rules (active and inactive) ordered by priority, lowest first, which is the order they are evaluated in. Filter with account_id to find every rule pointing at one GL account — the check to run before deactivating it. Returns {rules, total, auto_posting_rules, next_offset}: up to limit rules (default 75, max 75); when next_offset is not null, call again with offset=next_offset for the next page. total and auto_posting_rules count the WHOLE filtered set, not the page, so they answer "is any rule posting to this account" without paging.

account_id.description: Only rules posting to this GL account UUID

active_only.description: Default false — inactive rules are returned too, because a disabled rule is still a thing an agent needs to see.

search.description: Case-insensitive match on rule name or match pattern

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

tools.name: get_bank_rule
tools.description: Fetch one bank categorisation rule by id, including the GL account, supplier or customer it posts to.

tools.name: list_import_batches
tools.description: Bank statement import batches for this company, newest first — one row per statement file that import_bank_statement (or the app) landed. Each row carries transaction_count (rows written at import time), transactions_remaining (rows still linked now — undo_bank_import removes unallocated ones) and transactions_allocated (remaining rows with a posted journal). A batch with transactions_allocated > 0 cannot be fully undone; reverse those allocations first. Filter by bank_account_id to see one account. Returns at most 100 rows (default 20); there is no cursor — narrow by account for a long history.

tools.name: list_journals
tools.description: GL journal entries for this company in an entry-date window, across ALL accounts and sources (bank allocations, invoices, manual, auto-post), newest first. Unlike list_agent_postings it is not limited to MCP-created entries. status: draft = not yet posted; posted = in the ledger; reversed = posted entries that a contra has already been posted against. status=posted INCLUDES reversed entries (status never flips on reversal — reversed: true on the row is the only signal), so filter them out client-side or ask for status=reversed to see just those. account_id restricts to journals with at least one line on that account. include_lines=true adds each journal's lines (account code/name, debit, credit) — leave it off when scanning. limit is capped at 100 (default 50). Paging: the reply carries next_cursor whenever more rows match; call again with cursor set and every other argument unchanged until next_cursor is null. include_lines=true on 100 journals is unbounded (a payroll or bulk journal carries hundreds of lines) and can pass 90 KB: to size or total a window use detail="summary" (count of journals and total_debit over the WHOLE filter set, no rows) and group_by=source|month|status (groups sum to the totals; status is draft|posted|reversed, a reversed journal counts under reversed; at most 200 groups, the rest summed in other). A summary takes no cursor.

account_id.description: gl_accounts.id — only journals touching this account.

detail.description: summary = totals (and groups, with group_by) over the whole filter set, no rows. Default standard (rows).

group_by.description: Group the summary by one of: source, month, status. Implies detail "summary".

tools.name: list_bank_reconciliations
tools.description: Reconciliation sessions for the company, newest statement date first, with their status (in_progress or completed), statement and reconciled balances, the outstanding difference, and matched/unmatched transaction counts. Read-only. Filter to one account with bank_account_id (a GL account id from bank_accounts_status).

tools.name: list_practice_clients
tools.description: List the practice's clients (the firms it does work for). These are practice clients, NOT the AR customers returned by list_customers — a practice client is who time is booked against. Filter by status; default returns every status.

search.description: Matches legal name or trading name.

tools.name: list_job_categories
tools.description: List the practice's job categories — the top level of the two-level taxonomy a time entry is booked against (category → work item). Inactive categories are excluded unless include_inactive is true.

tools.name: list_work_items
tools.description: List work items — the second level of the time-entry taxonomy. A time entry REQUIRES a work item, and work items are NOT seeded when a company is set up, so a category with zero work items cannot be booked against. Omit category_id to audit every category at once; an empty result for a category is the signal to call create_work_item. Returns {work_items, total, next_offset}: up to limit rows (default 200, max 300); when next_offset is not null, call again with offset=next_offset for the next page. total is the whole match count, so total 0 is the "no work items" signal.

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's next_offset; omit for the first page.

tools.name: list_time_entries
tools.description: List logged time entries. Defaults to the calling user's own entries; pass all_users to see the whole practice. date_from/date_to are inclusive ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD). Each entry carries job_id: the job (engagement) it was booked against, or null — the id log_time_entry's job_id takes.
