tools.description: Apply an APPROVED credit note's unused credit to ONE document you name: a customer invoice for a customer credit note, a supplier bill for a supplier credit note. Use it when the note belongs to a specific invoice — approve_credit_note and auto_apply_unapplied apply oldest-first instead. The document must belong to the same customer/supplier as the note and be approved and unpaid — a draft, pending_approval, disputed, cancelled or paid document is refused. Applies the whole remainder by default, capped at the document's outstanding balance and at what the note's journal posted (a note with no live journal is refused); pass amount to apply less. Whatever is not applied stays on the note as on-account credit, and the note can be applied again to another document. Posts NO journal — the note's journal posted at approval; only balances move. Reversible with cancel_credit_note. A note applies to a given document once; change that amount with adjust_credit_note_application. Does NOT cover: draft notes (approve_credit_note), cash (apply_payment_to_supplier_invoice / apply_receipt_to_invoice). Run with dry_run first: it reports every balance that would move and writes nothing.

tools.name: cancel_supplier_invoice
tools.description: Cancel a supplier bill (supplier invoice). A draft, pending or disputed bill simply becomes cancelled. An APPROVED bill also has its approval journal (DR Expense/VAT, CR Accounts Payable) reversed by a contra entry dated like reverse_journal_entry dates it — the original date when its period is open, otherwise today — and both entries stay in the ledger. When that date is inside a locked (filed) VAT period and the journal carries VAT, the contra is dated forward to the first date outside every locked VAT period (reversal_date_roll says so). Refused, with the reason and the remedy named, when: anything is applied to the bill (void_payment / cancel_credit_note first); it is matched to a bank payment (reverse_bank_allocation first); a draft or approved payment still plans to pay it; another posted journal sourced from it stands (e.g. a DRC VAT journal — reverse_journal_entry first); its journal is still a draft; it is approved but has NO approval journal to reverse; no date up to today is outside the locked VAT periods for its VAT-carrying reversal; or it is already cancelled. Cancelling is final: there is no un-cancel; re-enter the bill if needed. Run with dry_run first: it shows the contra journal it would post and writes nothing.

tools.description: Delete a DRAFT credit note (customer or supplier) that was never approved, e.g. a duplicate or a mistake. It has no journal, so nothing posts and no balance moves. Owner or admin only. Attachments are detached (the files stay); nothing else is deleted. The delete is recorded in the audit trail. A deleted draft CANNOT be restored: the reply returns the note's values so create_credit_note can raise a fresh one (new id; a CN-year-number is issued as highest + 1, so deleting the latest frees its number). Adjustments: section_uplifts (turnover, cost_of_sales, other_income, operating_expense, other_expense) and account_uplifts override uplift_pct (account first); fixed_annual sets an account's annual total instead (shared over its dimension rows by the source's share); seasonality actuals (the source's monthly shape, default) or flat. Seasonality flat spreads over EVERY month of the target year. An account named in account_uplifts or fixed_annual must have a row in the source. tools.name: set_budget_amounts
tools.description: Set monthly budget amounts on one budget version. TRAPS FIRST: amounts are decimal STRINGS ("1250.00", at most 2 decimals), never numbers; months are YYYY-MM inside the version's financial year; an account is budgeted at ONE level per version (company level, or one cc1, cc2 or bu member; never two dimensions on one cell); a header account (budget its sub-accounts), an inactive one, or a non-income-statement account is refused per cell with the reason; a write is ALL OR NOTHING: one refused cell writes nothing. WORKFLOW: 1) dry_run true: answers what the save would ACTUALLY leave: counts (added, changed, removed, unchanged, recomputed, refused), the cells (paged: list_offset; a driver's recomputed dependents too), section totals per month before and after, and plan_hash; 2) the same call with dry_run false and that plan_hash (required when more than one cell is listed). If the budget or the request changed since, the call is refused ("plan changed since your dry run"): dry-run again. MODES: merge (default) sets the listed cells, amount null clears that cell; add adds amount to what the cell holds now; replace makes each listed ACCOUNT hold exactly the listed cells, clearing every other cell of that account in the version (any month or dimension; the way to move an account to another level); a reforecast's closed months are never cleared. At most 20000 changed cells per call (split larger writes; a call carries at most 100 000 argument values, so about 19 000 cells that each name a dimension). A budget holder writes only their own slices; a slice under review is refused. The save is a person's grid save as you (audited as you); restore_budget_version undoes the latest write while nobody has changed the version since. Needs write:budgets and read:reports. A person approves the version in IsaFlow.

tools.name: import_budget_workbook
tools.description: Import an edited budget template into its budget version: the app's Excel import, for an agent. WORKFLOW: list_budget_versions → get_budget_template → edit → import_budget_workbook dry_run true (the cells it changes, section totals before and after, warnings, conflicts, plan_hash) → the same call with dry_run false and that plan_hash → get_budget / budget_variance to check; restore_budget_version undoes the import while nobody has changed the version since. Send ONE of: rows, get_budget_template's JSON rows from any pages read at any time, in one call or several (each row: base EXACTLY as read, which ties it to its account and member and to the months it was read with; months: EVERY YYYY-MM of the year, a decimal string or null; account / dimension, if sent, must name the base's; other template fields are ignored; rows cannot be added: read the template row of the account; never pair a row's base with months from another read: a newer base on older months reverts what the newer read saw, listed by the dry run as changes, not conflicts), with grain, at most 2000 rows and 3 MB; or file_base64, an .xlsx as base64 (at most 2.9 million characters, about 2 MB of file: the MCP request is at most 3 MB): either the template from get_budget_template format xlsx, checked as the app checks an upload (its hidden _meta sheet, signed over the version, year, grain and _base, and its _base sheet, the amounts as downloaded, must be as IsaFlow wrote them; one with _meta but no _base is refused as tampered; another version's file or wrong month headers is refused whole), or a FREE-FORM sheet (no sheet named _meta or _base; any sheet whose name starts with "_" otherwise, look-alikes included, is refused): the sheet the workbook OPENS ON, which must be visible (the reply names it as sheet_name), with NO hidden row or column (filters included; a column under one character wide or a row under 3pt counts as hidden) and NO merged cell on or below its header row (a title merged above it is fine); a header row in rows 1 to 20 of the sheet with an account code column ("Account code", "Code" or "Account") and a column for EVERY month of the year (YYYY-MM, a date, or a month name with its year, or alone when it names one year month), at a cc1/cc2/bu grain (send grain) one dimension column, and only Account name, Name, Description, Section, Total, FY total, PY actual, Notes, Note or Dimension name besides (ignored; a second code-like header such as Account beside Account code is read as a name column); anything else, or the IsaFlow template's own header (a template without its hidden sheets: download a fresh one), is refused naming its sheet, row and column. EVERY AMOUNT ON A FREE-FORM SHEET IS ACCOUNTED FOR: a row with any month filled and a blank, error (#N/A) or unknown code refuses the import; only rows with every month empty and total rows (Total, Totals, Subtotal, Grand total as the code, or in the name column with no code) are skipped, and listed (skipped_rows, a total row with the amounts it held: CHECK them, they are not imported); a code typed as a NUMBER is read only in General or Text format and whole (format the code column as text), and one that lost a leading zero (a number 400 where the chart has 0400) is refused, never guessed. Free-form cells: a number is an amount only when its format is General, Text, a plain number format, or a South African rand currency / accounting format as Excel or LibreOffice write them; under a format showing exactly 2 decimals (the format section that draws the value: positive, or negative when it has one; the zero section never counts) a value with more is ROUNDED TO CENTS by IsaFlow's rule (15 significant digits, half away from zero; a spreadsheet may draw a value of 1e10 or more a cent differently) and listed in rounded_cells (rounded_count: CHECK them); under any other format it must be whole cents (a #,##0 cell holding cents is refused); formats that could change a value or its sign (scaling, literals, conditions, fill characters, dates, times, percents) are refused, and so is a conditional format on or below the header whose style sets a number format, font or fill; TRUE / FALSE, error and date cells are refused. A free-form sheet HAS NO BASE: it OVERWRITES. version_token is REQUIRED with it and must be the version's token now (dry run and live); every cell it names is then set to the sheet's value even if a colleague changed that cell after you read the token; a BLANK cell KEEPS its amount, the text "clear" clears the month, "0" is a budgeted zero. TRAPS FIRST (template and JSON grid): a cell changes only where the file differs from what was read (the .xlsx's _base, a JSON row's base), so a colleague's later save is never reverted; a cell changed both in the file and in the version since is a conflict (listed, with its member) and takes the file's value; null or a blank cell CLEARS that month (not budgeted), "0.00" is a budgeted zero; rows left out are untouched; version_token is optional there and checked on the LIVE call only. EVERY live import needs the plan_hash of its dry run, even one of a single cell: the dry run is the preview (as in the app), and a conflict shows there before anything is written. An unknown or ambiguous account or member, a non-income-statement account, a header or inactive account with no budget, an account budgeted at another level in this version (decision 4), a row listed twice or an amount that is not a decimal amount is refused PER ROW with the reason (i = the sheet row, or the 1-based position in rows); one refused row writes nothing (all or nothing). At most 20000 changed cells per call (split a bigger import into files of fewer rows; never chunked for you). A budget holder imports only their own slices; a slice under review, a locked version or a reforecast's closed months are refused by the grid save. THE DRY RUN IS THE VIEW TO CHECK: it lists every cell the import would change, with its value; a person confirms that before the live call. THE FREE-FORM GUARANTEE is about values, not appearance: each cell's stored value is read exactly, rounded only as above and listed; no value is invented, dropped or moved, and every money cell is accounted for; no cell the user cannot reach is read (hidden rows, columns or sheets, merges over data, a sheet other than the one the workbook opens on); anything it cannot read strictly is refused, not guessed. How a spreadsheet draws a cell (column width, fonts, fills, a renderer's rounding) is not part of it. A crafted file gives no capability beyond set_budget_amounts. An .xlsx is read in the server's spreadsheet slot: at most two per user at once, the same two places your own IsaFlow session uses (busy: try again in a moment); the JSON grid takes no slot. The save is a person's grid save as you (audited as you, in the version's history). Needs write:budgets and read:reports. A person approves the version in IsaFlow.

tools.name: restore_budget_version
tools.description: Undo the most recent MCP amount write (set_budget_amounts / set_budget_annual / import_budget_workbook) on a budget version: every cell it changed goes back to its value (and driver / typed source) before. TRAPS: only the version's MOST RECENT write, only while nobody has changed it since (the version token, its status and every cell of that write must be as the write left them; another save, an approve / lock / unlock or a driver recompute makes it refuse, naming the cells that differ), and only by whoever made the write or an owner or admin. WHAT IT COVERS: amount writes only. It never undoes set_budget_drivers (driver lines, planned hires, overrides, a headcount refresh) and refuses an amount write once any driver change was made at or after that write's transaction: in a later request, or anywhere in the same request (batch), including one made before the write. An override the write reset to a driver that now computes the same value cannot be pinned again: that restore is refused. An override no driver covers any more (its driver's range shrank) comes back as a manual figure with its value. Each write is restored at most once and a restore cannot itself be undone; once the latest write is restored, earlier writes cannot be. snapshot_id (from the write's reply) is optional and, when given, must be that most recent write. WORKFLOW: dry_run true checks it all, changes nothing and answers plan_hash; then dry_run false with that plan_hash (required when the write changed more than one cell). The restore is a grid save as you (audited as you). Needs write:budgets and read:reports.

tools.name: set_budget_drivers
tools.description: Change the drivers of one budget version: driver lines (set_driver, delete_driver), overrides (reset_override: a typed cell back to its driver), planned hires (add_hire, update_hire, delete_hire) and headcount (refresh_headcount). TRAPS FIRST: restore_budget_version does NOT undo this (it undoes amount writes only, and refuses one once drivers changed after it); the reply lists every driver line and hire as it was before, which is how to undo. One driver per row (account at one level: company, or one cc1, cc2 or bu member, the level the account is budgeted at in the version; never two dimensions); a driver writes only its months, never a closed (actual) month and never an override; set_driver replaces the row's driver; delete_driver turns the row's overrides into typed figures; a per_head driver reads payroll headcount on its own write and on refresh_headcount only. amount is a decimal STRING (rand per month, or per head); pct a number (4 decimals). delete_driver, update_hire and delete_hire name rows that exist before the call: a row or hire made by an earlier change of the same call cannot be named (call again). Refused on a locked version and, for a budget holder, outside their slices or in a slice under review. The changed amounts are the version's at once: get_three_way and the reports read the changed amounts. WORKFLOW: 1) dry_run true: the real changes rolled back, answering every cell they would change (other accounts' recomputed dependents included), section totals before and after, the driver lines and hires before and after, and plan_hash; 2) the same call with dry_run false and that plan_hash (always required). If the version changed since, it is refused: dry-run again. The recomputed values are not bound by plan_hash (a payroll headcount can move); the live reply lists what was written. At most 50 changes and 20000 changed cells per call, all or nothing. Each change is audited as you. Needs write:budgets and read:reports.

tools.name: create_fixed_asset
tools.description: Register a fixed asset on the asset register (the subledger): name, category, purchase date, cost, useful life, residual (salvage_value) and depreciation method. Same create as the app's New Asset page. IT POSTS NOTHING TO THE GENERAL LEDGER: no capitalisation journal, so no write:post is needed. The cost reaches the ledger through the supplier bill or journal that bought the asset; register the asset here separately. gl_asset_account_id (optional) is the fixed-asset COST account a disposal later credits: an active leaf account of this company with a fixed-asset subtype; without it the asset cannot be disposed until one is set in the app. It takes no cost centre / business unit, no supplier bill link and no opening accumulated depreciation: the create path has none of them. category is a fixed asset category code (computers, motor_vehicles, furniture, office_equipment, buildings, machinery, ...); it sets the SARS wear-and-tear rate and the asset number prefix (COMP-0001). useful_life_years is the accounting (IAS 16) life and is required. depreciation_method is straight_line (default), reducing_balance or sum_of_years. purchase_date cannot be in the future. The next run_depreciation depreciates the asset and posts the charge. UNDO: delete_fixed_asset removes it while it has no footprint; after a depreciation run it can only be disposed. ALWAYS CALL IT WITH dry_run: true FIRST: it runs every refusal the live call runs, returns the asset (with the number it would take) and any existing asset with the same name, date and cost, writes nothing and does not consume the idempotency key. dry_run defaults to FALSE: a call without it registers. It refuses an unknown or inactive category, a cost account that is not an active fixed-asset leaf account of this company, a cost that is not above zero or has more than 2 decimals, a salvage value above the cost, a life or method that is invalid, and a future or impossible date. There is no closed-period refusal: registering an asset touches no ledger period, so an asset bought in a closed year can be registered; depreciation for a closed period is refused by run_depreciation.

The asset row is locked while it is checked, so a depreciation run in flight either finishes first (and the delete then refuses) or finds the asset gone. Deleting is final. tools.name: update_supplier_invoice
tools.description: Edit a DRAFT supplier invoice (bill). Posts nothing. Send only the fields to change; `lines`, when sent, REPLACES every line and the subtotal, VAT and total are recomputed exactly as create_supplier_invoice computes them (amounts NET of VAT; tax_rate defaults the lines' rate and is accepted only with lines). Refused, with the reason, when: the bill is not a draft (approved bills: cancel_supplier_invoice, then re-enter); a posted journal (e.g. DRC VAT) is sourced from it; the total, supplier or number would change while a payment, credit note, approval request or matched statement line names the bill, or the supplier already has a live bill with that number; or the stored lines carry a purchase-order link, project, cost centre or VAT classification that replacing them would drop. A line that leaves out cc1 / cc2 / bu keeps the value every stored line shares; when the stored lines differ on one, name it on every line. A line of a bill raised from a bank-first slip that still names no cc1 / cc2 / bu takes the slip's provisional journal's dimensions when they match it; the result lists those as inherited_dimensions. due_date: when invoice_date or supplier_id changes and the bill's due date came from payment terms (not set by hand or taken from the document), it is re-dated by the terms a new bill gets (the payment_terms sent here, else the supplier's, else the company default) unless you send a different due_date, which is kept as set by hand; a due date set by hand or from the document never moves, and payment_terms alone does not re-date. The result lists it in changed when it was re-dated.

tax_rate.description: Default VAT % for the lines sent. Only with lines.

gl_account_id.description: Expense GL account UUID; defaults to the company default expense account

cc1.description: Optional CC1 = FNO / client (code, UUID or alias). Usually omit it: a CC2 derives its FNO, and naming a CC1 that disagrees is refused.

cc2.description: Optional CC2 = project (code, UUID or alias, e.g. "Ben Farms"). Sets the FNO through its parent. A cost-of-sales line without one is reported in dimension_warnings.

bu.description: Optional business unit = function (code, UUID), e.g. "MAINT".

tools.name: reapply_payment_terms
tools.description: Re-date OPEN supplier bills (draft, pending approval, approved, part-paid) to each SUPPLIER's own payment terms. The new due date is always the supplier's terms applied to the bill's invoice date, never the company default; suppliers with no terms set are skipped and listed (skipped_suppliers). ALWAYS preview first (dry_run true; writes nothing) and show the person the rows. Then call again with dry_run false and send back ONLY the rows the person confirmed, each as its preview row's invoice_id, new_due_date (as due_date), current_due_date and current_source. Rows with preselected=false (the date was set by hand or came from the document) must NOT be sent unless the person explicitly ticked them. Each bill is re-checked under lock when applied and skipped with a reason (not_found, not_open, date_changed, terms_not_set, terms_changed, already_dated) if its due date or its source, its terms or its status changed since the preview: a date set by hand since then is never overwritten. A written bill's due-date source becomes "terms". Previews list at most 2000 bills (truncated=true: narrow with supplier_id).

With dry_run true they are checked as the live call checks them and items_check says what each would do: update, date_changed, terms_changed, or not_listed (not in this preview: already on that date, closed, outside supplier_id, or past a truncated list).

tools.name: adjust_credit_note_application
tools.description: Change how much of an APPROVED credit note is applied to ONE document (document_id): a customer invoice for a customer note, a supplier bill for a supplier note. new_amount is what the note should have applied to that document afterwards: 0 takes the application back (as unapply_credit_note), less takes part of it back, more applies more (the document need not carry the note yet). Refused for a draft or cancelled note, a document of another customer/supplier, a document that is not approved, a note whose journal is missing or reversed, and an unchanged amount. Posts NO journal: the note's journal posted at approval (returned as credit_note_journal_id); only balances move. Undo by calling again with new_amount = applied_before. Run with dry_run first: it reports every balance that would move and writes nothing.

tools.name: reverse_bank_allocation_batch
tools.description: Undo a whole bulk allocation: reverses the posted journal behind every transaction in the batch and returns them all to unallocated. The batch holds only the lines that actually POSTED — anything the allocate call skipped was never part of it and is not touched here. ALL OR NOTHING — if any reversal fails, none of them are applied. Transactions that have moved on since the batch posted (already reversed, or re-allocated to a different journal) are left untouched and listed in "skipped". The originals and their reversals both remain in the audit trail. A customer receipt whose unapplied cash a customer refund has already returned is refused (reverse the refund first, or include it in the same batch). By default each reversing journal carries its ORIGINAL entry's date when that period is still open, and today when it is closed; pass reversal_date to date every reversal in the batch explicitly.

reversal_date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD date for the reversing journal. Omit it and the reversal takes the ORIGINAL entry's date when that period is still open, falling back to today when it is closed — which keeps the correction in the period it corrects. Give a date to override that, typically to correct a closed month from the current open one. It may not be earlier than the entry being reversed, and its fiscal period must already exist and be open — a date in a year with no fiscal periods is refused, not posted.

tools.name: post_reclassification_batch
tools.description: Move posted amounts from one GL account to another, as one reversible batch. RUN propose_reclassification FIRST, or call this with dry_run: true — it returns exactly what would post and writes nothing. HOW IT WORKS: it POSTS A NEW JOURNAL — a contra on the source account and the same amount re-applied to the target, one pair per source line — and leaves every original posted line untouched. Nothing is edited or deleted. Each journal is a normal posted entry, so the batch is undone with reverse_journal_entry on the ids returned, and both the original and the correction stay in the audit trail. THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS MOST. If the source account is missing only an account_subtype, this is probably the WRONG remedy: setting the subtype with update_gl_account gets it into the classified bands of every report and moves nothing, while this merges the source account into the target permanently — after it, no report can tell the two apart. On real books most unclassified accounts are correctly named and correctly loaded, and moving them collapses distinct costs (direct material, sub-contractors, wayleave) into one line. The response warns with subtype_remedy_available and collapses_named_accounts when either applies; read them. PERIODS: with no posting_date each journal is dated at its own source line, so nothing crosses periods — and any line whose own fiscal period is CLOSED is skipped, because a closed period cannot be posted into. Pass posting_date to post the whole batch on one open day instead; the closed month then keeps its original classification and this period carries the correction. SKIPS versus FAILURES: a line the data will not let you move — closed period, no fiscal period, a reversed entry, already moved by an earlier batch, the contra leg of one — is SKIPPED with a reason and does not cost the rest. Anything else fails the WHOLE batch and nothing is posted. At most 500 source lines per call; narrow with from/to rather than have a batch truncate. A call with nothing left to move posts nothing and opens no batch.

source_account_id.description: GL account UUID the amounts currently sit on.

target_account_id.description: GL account UUID they should sit on instead. Must differ from the source.

from.description: Only consider source lines whose journal is dated on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit for no lower bound. Use from/to to keep a batch under 500 lines.

to.description: Only consider source lines dated on or before this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

posting_date.description: Date EVERY reclassification journal on this one day instead of on its own source line's date. This is how a closed month is corrected from an open one — and it MOVES THE CHARGE BETWEEN PERIODS: the closed month keeps the original classification and this period carries the correction. Omit it and each journal is dated at its source line, which is period-neutral but skips every line whose own period is closed.

tools.name: import_bank_statement
tools.description: Import a bank statement (OFX, CSV, QIF or MT940) into a bank account. A statement reference is stored WHERE THE FORMAT CARRIES ONE — the generic and ABSA header CSV layouts (a Reference column), FNB CSV, OFX, QIF and MT940 — and is then what bank_reference resolves against in allocate_bank_transaction and reverse_bank_allocation. The Standard Bank, Capitec and Nedbank CSV layouts and the legacy positional ABSA layout carry no reference column at all, so rows imported from those resolve by transaction_id only. Transactions already present are skipped by a (date, amount, description, balance) content hash — the reference is NOT part of it, so two same-day rows with the same amount, description and balance still collapse into one even when their references differ, so re-sending the same statement is safe. Note the flip side: two genuinely separate transactions on the same day with the same amount and description hash alike, and the second will be skipped as a duplicate — reconcile the closing balance after importing rather than trusting the row count. Creates transactions only: it posts no journals and does not touch transactions it did not create. Allocate afterwards with allocate_bank_transaction. Use dry_run to see what would land before writing.

tools.name: merge_gl_accounts
tools.description: Merge one GL account into another: every journal line on the source is repointed to the target, the source's child accounts are moved onto the target with their levels shifted, and the source is DEACTIVATED carrying zero. Nothing is deleted and no journal is posted — a repoint changes no debit and no credit, only which account carries it, so the company trial balance is identical afterwards. Per-account balances, comparatives and any report grouped by account DO change, for every period the moved lines touch. DOCUMENT LINES MOVE WITH IT: bill lines (supplier_invoice_items), customer invoice lines (customer_invoice_items), expense-claim lines, purchase-order lines (po_items) and capture events coded to the source are repointed to the target in the same transaction, only this company's rows. The dry run reports how many per table (documentRowsToRepoint), the live result reports the same counts (documentRowsRepointed), and the gl_account_merges record lists every moved row id per table (moved_document_rows). REFUSES (target_refused_for_open_bill_lines) when the target is an account bill lines may not use — a control, bank, VAT, system or header account, header including one that takes the source's children — and a bill not yet approved or posted has lines on the source: it could never be approved after the move. The refusal names the bills; recode their lines first. REFUSES (target_refused_for_open_invoice_lines) likewise when the target is or would become a header account and a customer invoice not yet approved or posted has lines on the source; it names the invoices. Bill lines coded while the merge runs are serialised: the bill-line guard takes FOR SHARE on the account row the merge holds FOR UPDATE, so that request waits, then sees the source inactive and is refused (or it finished first, and its line is moved). Expense-claim lines and PO lines are now serialised the same way (gl/documentLineAccountGuard.ts, FOR SHARE, before the first write). Capture events need no such guard: postJournalEntry refuses an inactive account (assertNoInactiveAccountLines) before it turns a draft into a posted entry, so a receipt whose resolved account was deactivated by a concurrent merge is caught there, whether it auto-posts immediately or waits as a draft. Built for a chart that carries two control accounts for one role — a Sage-imported account holding the old population beside the one the write path actually posts to. There is no canonical control account in this schema and the codes differ per company, so this tool takes both accounts by id and forms no opinion about which is canonical. RUN dry_run FIRST and read it. It returns both accounts' figures derived by separate queries, the trial balance either side of the move, the journal entries as ids you can open, every row that would not move with a reason code, the child accounts that would be reparented, and what breaks if the proposal is wrong. It writes nothing. REFUSES: the same account twice; two different account_types; a target sitting below the source in the chart (a cycle); a SYSTEM account as the source, because auto-posting resolves those by subtype and deactivating one leaves the role unclaimed; a bank-subtype source that bank transactions still reference; and a source any configuration row still names (bank rules, AFS mappings, asset categories, products — the check is driven by the foreign-key catalogue, so it covers tables added after this tool was written). Every foreign-key reference other than the journal lines and the four document-line columns above still blocks the merge. SKIPS BLOCK THE MERGE: a posted line in a closed fiscal period, or a posted line with no fiscal period at all, is reported with its amount and the whole merge refuses. A control-account merge that leaves part of its balance behind is worse than one that does not run. ALSO REFUSES a merge that crosses a REPORTING CLASS: vat (subtypes vat_input, vat_output, tax — what the VAT201 selects on) and bank (what the banking screens reach statement rows through) are each their own class, and everything else including NULL is ordinary. Crossing that boundary puts money that is not tax onto a SARS return in one direction and drops it off in the other, with the trial balance identical either way. Same-class merges are allowed, so the two control-account cases this tool was built for (NULL to receivable, NULL to payable) pass. Does NOT cover: configuration rows (repoint them yourself first) — and note that the configuration sweep reads foreign keys, so a reference held BY ACCOUNT CODE rather than by id is invisible to it. group_accounts.account_code is the known case: the consolidation chart resolves by code, the source keeps its code after the merge, so the group mapping goes on resolving to an account that now carries zero while the money joins the target's consolidation line. Check it by hand before merging an account that is in a group. It also does not rename or renumber the chart, and never merges across companies. CONCURRENCY: the live call locks both accounts for the rest of the request. If another request holds one, this waits 5 seconds and then refuses with a message saying to retry — that one is safe to re-issue with the same idempotency_key, because nothing was written. One failure mode is NOT specific: if the ledger changes between the preview and the write (a journal posted, a period closed), the merge aborts having written nothing, but reaches you as a generic failure rather than a named one. Re-run with dry_run to see what moved.

tools.name: create_supplier_invoice
tools.description: Create a DRAFT supplier invoice (bill / accounts payable document). Posts nothing to the ledger — use approve_supplier_invoice (needs write:post) to post DR Expense + DR VAT Input / CR Accounts Payable. Line amounts are NET of VAT: tax_rate is applied on top of quantity x unit_price. A line with no gl_account_id posts to the company's default expense account. Resolve supplier_id with list_suppliers and gl_account_id with list_gl_accounts first. Pass external_system + external_ref (e.g. the Sage id) to make the create idempotent: a live bill already carrying them is returned instead (already_existed: true). With an external_ref, a supplier's invoice_number may repeat an existing bill's (a supplier that reused its number on a different document); without one, a repeated number is refused.

due_date.description: When omitted: from this bill's own payment_terms when you give them ('netNN' or 'immediate'), else the supplier's terms (see list_suppliers), else the company's default terms. A given date is kept even where it differs from the supplier's own terms; that comes back in due_date_warnings. Omit it unless the supplier's document states it.

With external_system, makes the create IDEMPOTENT: if a live record of this kind already carries the same (external_system, external_ref), it is returned with already_existed: true and nothing is written.

tools.name: approve_supplier_invoice
tools.description: Approve a DRAFT supplier invoice and POST it to the ledger — DR Expense (per line) + DR VAT Input / CR Accounts Payable. Irreversible except by a reversing entry. Requires the write:post permission. The invoice must be in draft or pending_approval; anything else is refused with its current status. Budget check: under the company's block policy a bill over its remaining budget, or with a line outside every budgeted slice of a budgeted account (e.g. no cost centre where the account is budgeted per cost centre), is refused (BUDGET_EXCEEDED, naming each line; an agent cannot override); under warn it posts and those lines come back as budget_warnings.

allow_late_input_claim.description: Only when the posting is dated inside a LOCKED (filed) VAT period and its only VAT is INPUT VAT: true claims that VAT late, in the next open VAT period (VAT Act s16(3)) — the journal keeps its date, a companion journal on the first day after the lock claims the VAT, and the result carries late_claim. Output VAT, a reduction of input VAT, a claim over five years late or into a closed period is still refused. Omit it to be refused inside a locked period as usual.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: bulk_create_supplier_invoices
tools.description: Create up to 100 DRAFT supplier invoices (bills) in ONE call. Each element takes the same payload as create_supplier_invoice, without its idempotency_key. Posts nothing to the ledger — approve each with approve_supplier_invoice (needs write:post). ALL OR NOTHING for faults: if an element genuinely fails, none of them are created, so a retry on the same idempotency_key is safe. A REPEAT IS NOT A FAULT: two elements with the same (supplier_id, invoice_number) are one bill sent twice — the first is created, the later ones are listed in "skipped" with a reason, and the rest of the batch still runs. Note this is an in-batch check only: the database accepts the same invoice_number twice, so a bill already in the books is NOT detected here. Resolve supplier_id with list_suppliers and gl_account_id with list_gl_accounts first.

invoice_number.description: The supplier's own invoice number. Refused over 50 characters.

due_date.description: When omitted: from this bill's own payment_terms ('netNN' or 'immediate') when given, else the supplier's terms, else the company's default terms. A given date is kept even where it differs from the supplier's own terms; that comes back in due_date_warnings. Omit it unless the supplier's document states it.

cc1.description: Optional CC1 = FNO / client (code, UUID or alias). Usually omit it: a CC2 derives its FNO, and naming a CC1 that disagrees is refused.

cc2.description: Optional CC2 = project (code, UUID or alias, e.g. "Ben Farms"). Sets the FNO through its parent. A cost-of-sales line without one is reported in dimension_warnings.

bu.description: Optional business unit = function (code, UUID), e.g. "MAINT".

The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: bulk_approve_supplier_invoices
tools.description: Approve and POST up to 100 DRAFT supplier invoices (bills) in ONE call — each posts DR Expense (per line) + DR VAT Input / CR Accounts Payable. Irreversible except by a reversing entry. Requires the write:post permission. Identify each bill by its invoice_id (from list_supplier_invoices or bulk_create_supplier_invoices). A bill that cannot be approved is SKIPPED, not a failure: not found, already approved, cancelled, or dated in a CLOSED fiscal period — each is listed in "skipped" with its reason and the rest of the batch still posts. Budget check: under the company's block policy a bill over its remaining budget, or with a line outside every budgeted slice of a budgeted account, is skipped as "budget_exceeded" (an agent cannot override; a person can, on the bill in the app); under warn it posts and those lines come back as budget_warnings. ALL OR NOTHING for real faults: if a bill genuinely fails to post, the whole batch is rolled back, nothing is posted, and the error names the element. A repeated invoice_id is REFUSED (not skipped) — each bill may appear once. Every posting is attributed to the agent and visible in list_agent_postings. Use dry_run to see what would post and what would be skipped.

invoice_ids.description: The bills to approve — at most 100, each named once.

dry_run.description: Report what would post and what would be skipped, and write nothing.

Reserves an invoice number for each; posts nothing to the GL — approve each with finalize_invoice (needs write:post). ALL OR NOTHING: if any element is rejected or fails, none of them are created, so a retry on the same idempotency_key is safe.

gl_account_id.description: Revenue account to credit (a leaf, active revenue account). Omit for the default sales account.

project_id.description: Job (a `projects` id — what Project Profitability reads) the line's revenue belongs to. Not the CC2 project: that is `cc2`.

cc1.description: Optional CC1 = FNO / client (code, UUID or alias). Usually omit it: a CC2 derives its FNO, and naming a CC1 that disagrees is refused.

cc2.description: Optional CC2 = project (code, UUID or alias, e.g. "Ben Farms"). Sets the FNO through its parent. A cost-of-sales line without one is reported in dimension_warnings.

bu.description: Optional business unit = function (code, UUID), e.g. "MAINT".

project_id.description: The invoice's project, display only; tag lines to post by project (items[].project_id).

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: void_receipt
tools.description: Void a customer receipt (CP document): takes the cash back off every invoice it was applied to, reverses its journal, and cancels the document. If the receipt settled a bank line, that line returns to unallocated too. Use to correct a receipt captured in error — the original and its reversal both remain in the audit trail. Requires the write:post permission. Already-cancelled documents are refused, and so is a receipt whose unapplied cash a customer refund has already returned (reverse the refund first).

reversal_date.description: Date for the reversing journal. Defaults to the original entry's date when that period is open, today when it is closed.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: void_payment
tools.description: Void a supplier payment: takes the cash back off every bill it was applied to, reverses its journal, and cancels the document. If the payment settled a bank line, that line returns to unallocated too. Use to correct a payment captured in error — the original and its reversal both remain in the audit trail. Requires the write:post permission. Already-cancelled documents are refused. undo_share: true with share_journal_id ALSO undoes, per bill the payment settled, the share a person took out of a CONTRA payment's clearing account (the journal that reversed the bill's expense and input VAT against it): one journal per bill, DR the bill's expense legs (with their dimensions) + VAT Input / CR the clearing account, for what THIS payment applied to the bill, split pro rata over the bill's own posting, dated on the share journal's date (refused, never rolled, when that period is closed or VAT-locked), reference undo-share:<payment_id>:<bill_id>; a second undo of the same bill and payment is refused. Posted after the void in the same call; each is reversible with reverse_journal_entry. Refused unless the payment is a contra and the share journal still HOLDS what is undone — cumulatively: its debit on the clearing account and its credit on each bill account, less every earlier live undo of that share. A share that debits the clearing account by more than this payment applied carries other bills: then undo_amounts (how much of each bill it reversed, from the share's own working) is required. Hand undos count against what the share holds, like an earlier undo: ANY journal not linked to a share, dated in the share's month or a bill's month, that credits the clearing account and debits the share's accounts — counted GROSS (a correction netting the clearing account to nil still counts), netted only with its own reversals — even one that undid a different share or bill. Another REVERSED journal of the share's shape (debits the clearing account, credits the share's accounts; any source) dated on or after the earliest undone bill or the share — a share re-dated by reverse-and-repost — refuses the undo outright. Either can refuse a legitimate undo; then post that undo by hand. A hand undo dated outside both months is not seen. Only a manual journal (entered, imported or recurring) can be a share, and an undo is linked to its share by source record, not by its reference text. Also refused: a late-claimed bill and a deactivated account. A share with live undos cannot be reversed (re-dating a share by reverse-and-repost): reverse its undos first. The undo journals carry no source document, so the pre-filing VAT input check lists their VAT Input lines as no_document; the bill is the evidence. Under manual-journal approval enforcement a matching rule refuses the call (a person must enter it). undo_share also needs the write:journals permission. Run with dry_run first: it performs the whole call and rolls it back, writing nothing.

reversal_date.description: Date for the reversing journal. Defaults to the original entry's date when that period is open, today when it is closed.

undo_share.description: Also undo the share a person took out of the contra's clearing account for each bill it settled: posts DR the bill's expense legs + VAT Input / CR the clearing account, per bill, dated on share_journal_id's date. Only for a contra payment (its journal credits a clearing account, not a bank). Requires share_journal_id.

share_journal_id.description: The posted journal that took the bills' expense and VAT out of the clearing account (DR clearing / CR expense + VAT Input) — e.g. the month's re-dated share journal. It must debit the clearing account and credit every account the undo debits by at least the amounts undone, or the call is refused.

undo_amounts.description: How much of each of this payment's bills the share journal reversed, when the share carries other bills too (it debits the clearing account by more than this payment applied — then this is REQUIRED, because the share's lines do not say which bill each amount belongs to). Each amount is at most what this payment applied to that bill; a bill left out is not undone. Omit when the share covers exactly this payment's bills. The figures are TRUSTED: they must come from the share journal's own working (which bills it reversed, and how much of each) — the share's lines do not say, and only its per-account totals can be checked.

dry_run.description: Run the whole void (and undo) and roll it back: answers what would change, or the refusal the live call would give, and writes nothing.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: create_bank_rule
tools.description: Create a bank categorisation rule. It applies to transactions matched from now on — creating a rule does NOT post anything by itself. auto_create_entry=true means every future match posts a journal automatically without review and requires the "Post to ledger" permission (write:post); leave it false unless that is what you want. dry_run=true validates and previews without writing. Where the company requires approval of bank-rule changes, an auto-posting rule is held for a person to approve (status pending_approval). Check list_bank_rules first: a more specific rule with a lower priority wins, and two rules matching the same pattern is how a migration gets silently undone.

gl_account_id.description: GL account the rule posts to

auto_create_entry.description: TRUE means a match POSTS a journal automatically and requires write:post. Default false.

auto_apply.description: What an auto-posted supplier or customer line does with its cash. "fifo" (the default) applies it to that contact's OLDEST open documents; "none" creates the payment or receipt and leaves the cash on account. Only meaningful with auto_create_entry.

dry_run.description: Validate and preview only; writes nothing.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: update_bank_rule
tools.description: Update a bank categorisation rule. Pass only the fields to change. Re-pointing gl_account_id is the fix for a rule that still routes to a retired account. Setting auto_create_entry=true, or changing any other field while the stored rule keeps auto_create_entry=true, requires the "Post to ledger" permission (write:post). Setting auto_create_entry=false does not. dry_run=true validates and previews without writing. To only stop a rule firing, use disable_bank_rule — it needs nothing but the id.

gl_account_id.description: GL account the rule posts to

auto_create_entry.description: TRUE means a match POSTS a journal automatically and requires write:post. Default false.

auto_apply.description: What an auto-posted supplier or customer line does with its cash. "fifo" (the default) applies it to that contact's OLDEST open documents; "none" creates the payment or receipt and leaves the cash on account. Only meaningful with auto_create_entry.

dry_run.description: Validate and preview only; writes nothing.

It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: disable_bank_rule
tools.description: Deactivate a bank categorisation rule so it stops matching. The rule is kept, not deleted — pass enable=true to turn it back on. Reactivating a rule with auto_create_entry=true requires the "Post to ledger" permission (write:post). This is the safe way to stop a rule that posts to an account you are retiring.

enable.description: Default false (disable). true re-activates the rule.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: reverse_allocations
tools.description: Reverse EVERY allocation in one bank account between two dates, inclusive — including allocations made by bank rules or by an import, which carry no batch_id and cannot be reversed by reverse_bank_allocation_batch. ALL OR NOTHING: if any reversal fails, none are applied, so the account is never left half-unwound. Refuses (it does not truncate) if the range holds more than 500 allocated transactions — narrow the dates. Run with dry_run=true first: it reports exactly which transactions would be reversed, with the rule that created each one, and writes nothing. Unallocated, excluded and already-reversed transactions in the range are not touched. A customer receipt whose unapplied cash a customer refund has already returned is refused (reverse the refund first, or include it in the range). Requires the write:post permission.

bank_account_id.description: The bank GL account UUID (from bank_accounts_status or list_gl_accounts).

dry_run.description: true reports what would be reversed and writes nothing. Do this first.

reversal_date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD date for the reversing journal. Omit it and the reversal takes the ORIGINAL entry's date when that period is still open, falling back to today when it is closed — which keeps the correction in the period it corrects. Give a date to override that, typically to correct a closed month from the current open one. It may not be earlier than the entry being reversed, and its fiscal period must already exist and be open — a date in a year with no fiscal periods is refused, not posted.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: set_opening_balance
tools.description: Post an opening balance for a bank account so it reconciles from a known starting point — for a card or account whose earlier history was never captured. Posts a real journal dated as_at (DR the bank account and CR the contra for a positive amount, reversed for a negative one) and records the figure on the account so the banking screens agree with the ledger. contra_account_id is optional: omitted, the other side posts to the company's Opening Balance Equity clearing account (created on first use), which should net to zero once every opening balance is captured — the close-readiness checklist warns while it does not. Pass an explicit contra_account_id (retained earnings, a suspense account) only when the firm's policy says so. The reply carries the contra actually used. Refuses if the account already has an opening balance — reverse that journal first rather than stacking a second one. Requires the write:post permission.

as_at.description: The date the balance is stated as at. The journal carries this date, so its fiscal period must exist and be open.

amount.description: The balance as at that date. Negative for an overdrawn account. Zero is refused — it would post nothing and tell you it succeeded.

contra_account_id.description: Optional. The other side of the entry. Defaults to the company's Opening Balance Equity account.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: attach_document
tools.description: Attach a document (JPEG, PNG or PDF — a receipt, slip or invoice scan) to a bank transaction, named by transaction_id or by bank_reference (plus bank_account_id to narrow an ambiguous reference). content is the file as base64 (a data: URL is also accepted). Maximum 750 KB of file bytes per call — larger files must be reduced before sending. The declared mime_type is checked against the file's real bytes and refused on mismatch. Posts nothing and changes no allocation; the same file sent twice under different idempotency keys is stored twice.

bank_reference.description: Statement reference, as an alternative to transaction_id.

content.description: Base64 file bytes, or a data:<mime>;base64,… URL.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: attach_entity_document
tools.description: Attach a supporting document to ANY accounting document, named by entity_type and entity_id: supplier_invoice, customer_invoice, credit_note, supplier_payment, customer_payment, or bank_transaction (a bank line). Use this for a supplier's tax invoice on a bill, a remittance on a receipt, a credit note scan, a slip on a bank line. A bank transaction is routed to its own store for you (it needs write:bank-tx as well as write:invoices, takes PDF, JPEG or PNG only, and keeps no document_type or notes); attach_document does the same for a bank line named by its statement reference. content is the file as base64 (a data: URL is also accepted). Accepts PDF, JPEG, PNG, DOCX, XLSX; maximum 2 MB of file bytes per call. The declared mime_type is checked against the file's real bytes and refused on mismatch. If the entity already holds an active document with the same file name and size, nothing is stored and that document comes back with duplicate: true, so a bulk back-fill can be re-run safely. extract (default false) runs the background text extraction on the file. Posts nothing.

entity_id.description: UUID of the bill, invoice, credit note, payment or bank transaction.

document_type.description: Default "invoice" for invoices and bills, "credit_note_doc" for credit notes, "proof_of_payment" for payments.

content.description: Base64 file bytes, or a data:<mime>;base64,… URL.

notes.description: Optional, e.g. the source ("Sage SIV0005104 attachment").

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: cancel_bank_reconciliation
tools.description: Cancel an in-progress reconciliation: the session is deleted and every transaction it claimed is released back to the bank account. Matches made inside the session are undone (those rows return to "imported"); allocated, provisional and excluded rows keep their status and their journal entries and are only detached — nothing is removed from the GL. A completed reconciliation cannot be cancelled. Use dry_run to see how many transactions would be released before committing.

reconciliation_id.description: Id from list_bank_reconciliations. Must be in_progress.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: reopen_bank_reconciliation
tools.description: Reopen a COMPLETED reconciliation so a wrong allocation inside it can be corrected. The session goes back to in_progress and every line completion marked reconciled returns to the state it had: allocated lines (they carry an allocation) to "allocated", matched lines to "matched". Nothing is posted and no journal changes. While it is open, an allocated line can be reversed with reverse_bank_allocation (it leaves the session with its reversal); complete it again by running perform_bank_reconciliation on the same statement after cancel_bank_reconciliation, or complete the open session in the app. NEWEST FIRST: only the latest completed reconciliation on an account can be reopened — a statement opens at the closing balance of the one before, so reopening an older one under later sign-offs is refused and the refusal names how many later ones stand. Also refused when a session is already in progress on the account. reason is stored on the reconciliation as the audit record. dry_run runs every guard and reports how many lines would be restored, writing nothing. Requires the write:post permission.

reconciliation_id.description: Id from list_bank_reconciliations. Must be completed and the latest on its account.

reason.description: Why it is being reopened. Stored on the reconciliation.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: create_job_category
tools.description: Create a job category — the top level of the time-entry taxonomy. A category on its own cannot be booked against: create_work_item must add at least one work item under it before time can be logged. Names are unique per company, case- and whitespace-insensitively; a clash is refused and the reply names the existing id.

reporting_tag.description: Optional grouping label used by practice reports.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: create_work_item
tools.description: Create a work item under a job category — the second level of the time-entry taxonomy, and the one log_time_entry requires. Work items are NOT seeded when a company is set up, so a category returning an empty list_work_items needs this before any time can be booked against it. Names are unique within a category, case- and whitespace-insensitively. default_billable seeds the entry's billable flag and defaults to true.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: log_time_entry
tools.description: Log a draft time entry against a practice client, job category and work item. All three ids are required and must be active and consistent — the work item must belong to the category. Resolve them with list_practice_clients / list_job_categories / list_work_items first. Without allow_backdating, entry_date must fall in the current or previous calendar month. The entry is created as a DRAFT and is booked to the calling user; submit_time_entries moves it into the approval flow. The rate is resolved server-side from the staff/client rate table and is not accepted as an argument. Use dry_run to validate without writing.

entry_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Cannot be in the future.

task_description.description: What was actually done. Max 500 characters.

job_id.description: Optional job (engagement) to book the time against: an open job of practice_client_id, refused if the job is complete, cancelled or billed. Take it from list_time_entries (job_id on an earlier entry) or the job's id in the app. Its Engagement Budget is spent by this entry.

allow_backdating.description: Required to book into any month before the previous calendar month. Such a period has usually been invoiced and reported on; the entry would restate those reports, and it carries the rate effective on that date rather than today's.

dry_run.description: Validate everything and report the rate that would apply, without writing.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: submit_time_entries
tools.description: Submit draft time entries for approval. Only the calling user's own DRAFT entries are affected — ids belonging to another user, or already past draft, are skipped rather than refused, and the reply reports which. This moves hours into the approval flow that feeds WIP and client invoicing.

entry_ids.description: Time entry UUIDs from list_time_entries. Max 200.

dry_run.description: Report which ids would be submitted, without writing.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: create_credit_note
tools.description: Create a DRAFT credit note. Posts nothing to the ledger — use approve_credit_note (needs write:post) to post it. type "customer" credits a customer and needs client_id (from list_customers); type "supplier" credits a supplier bill and needs supplier_id (from list_suppliers). subtotal is NET of VAT and must be positive — tax_rate (default 15) is applied on top, and total = subtotal + VAT. Optionally link the note to the invoice it corrects with customer_invoice_id / supplier_invoice_id; a LINKED note is AUTO-APPLIED at approve, reducing that invoice's outstanding balance by up to its outstanding amount. Leave the link out to raise standalone credit. An identical open draft (same counterparty, linked invoice, date and amount) is REFUSED and its id returned — retrying with a new idempotency_key will not create a second one. When it is genuinely a SECOND credit (two returns on one day for one amount), call again with duplicate_of set to the id the refusal named. A supplier note linked to a bill credits that bill's own expense accounts and CC1/CC2/BU pro rata at approve; mirror_bill also takes its VAT from the bill as it stands now (see document_vat_history). Pass external_system + external_ref (e.g. the Sage RTN id) to make the create idempotent: a live note already carrying them is returned instead (already_existed: true).

client_id.description: Customer UUID — required when type is "customer"

supplier_id.description: Supplier UUID — required when type is "supplier"

customer_invoice_id.description: Invoice this note credits; auto-applied at approve

supplier_invoice_id.description: Supplier invoice this note credits; auto-applied at approve

gl_account_id.description: Supplier notes only: the GL account credited when the note is not linked to a bill, or for what the expense lines of the linked bill can no longer take (a linked note reverses the accounts and CC1/CC2/BU of that bill first). Omitted: the default expense account.

duplicate_of.description: Only after a refusal: the id of the identical open draft it named, confirming this is a second, separate credit.

mirror_bill.description: Supplier notes only, needs supplier_invoice_id, excludes tax_rate. The note's VAT is taken from the bill AS IT STANDS NOW: subtotal x the VAT its posting, reversals and credit notes leave / the base they leave, other open drafts on the bill netted off (see document_vat_history). The expense side mirrors the bill at approve whether or not this is set. Refused when the subtotal is more than the bill still carries, and — unless acknowledge_vat_already_reversed — when the bill's VAT is out of proportion to its base or a journal naming the bill moved its VAT (a second reversal would misstate the VAT201). Approval re-checks the note against the bill.

acknowledge_vat_already_reversed.description: Only with mirror_bill, after its VAT_ALREADY_REVERSED refusal, once you have checked the journals it names are about this bill. Needs vat_amount.

tools.name: approve_credit_note
tools.description: Approve a DRAFT credit note and POST it to the ledger. Requires the write:post permission. Customer note: DR Revenue + DR VAT Output / CR Accounts Receivable. Supplier note: DR Accounts Payable / CR Expense + CR VAT Input. Approving also APPLIES the note. A linked invoice is settled first, capped at its outstanding balance; the REMAINDER is then applied FIFO to that same customer's or supplier's other open documents, oldest first. Pass auto_apply "linked" to skip the FIFO walk and apply only to the linked document (nothing, if there is no link), or "none" to apply NOTHING, not even to the linked document: the note posts and the whole credit stays on account for apply_credit_note. The resulting status is DERIVED: "approved" when nothing was applied, "partially_applied" when some of the face value is still on account, "applied" when all of it was consumed. applied_amount is what was consumed and applied_to_invoice_ids names every document it settled. Whatever is left is on-account credit, which aged_debtors / aged_creditors report as unapplied and net off. Reverse the whole thing with cancel_credit_note.

tools.name: cancel_credit_note
tools.description: Cancel a credit note. Requires the write:post permission. An approved, partially applied or applied note: REVERSES its journal entry with a reversing entry (the original stays posted) and un-applies the credit from EVERY document it was applied to — each one's amount_paid drops back and its status is recomputed, in the same transaction. A DRAFT note is cancelled WITHOUT a journal: it is set to cancelled, nothing is posted or reversed, no balance moves and the number stays on the books (no gap). That is the way out for a draft that cannot be deleted (delete_draft_credit_note refuses one numbered from the supplier return sequence). A draft is refused when it carries a journal or applied credit (inconsistent data), when a dispute resolution raised it, or when it has a pending approval request. A cancelled note stays cancelled. Run with dry_run first: it runs the real cancel and rolls it back, so it refuses exactly what the live call would, and writes nothing.

tools.name: post_payroll_journal
tools.description: Post the general-ledger journal for an APPROVED payroll run: debit labour cost with gross pay plus the employer UIF and SDL the company owes on top of it, and credit PAYE payable, UIF payable (both halves), SDL payable, any voluntary deductions, and net pay. This is the entry that is missing from these books. Today net pay alone is coded to Salaries & Wages, so employment cost is understated by every employer contribution and no PAYE, UIF or SDL liability is ever raised. ALWAYS call it with dry_run: true first. The preview returns the complete journal — every line, both totals, the fiscal period the date falls in, and the run totals it was derived from — and it applies every check the live call applies: the run must be approved, it must not already carry a journal, the four required GL accounts (5200 labour, 2140 PAYE, 2150 UIF, 2160 SDL) must exist, an active account must hold the bank system role of the company (net pay is credited to it, whatever its code; missing_bank_account otherwise) unless a Payroll net pay account is set in Default Accounts (see below), account 2175 must exist if there are voluntary deductions, no target account may be deactivated (inactive_target_account — the ledger refuses the posting; it does not activate them), the fiscal period covering the date must be open, the run must have something to post, and the journal must balance to the cent. If any of those fails, BOTH the preview and the live call refuse and name the reason. When the company has set a Payroll net pay account in Default Accounts (a clearing liability such as 2170 Net Salaries Payable, for companies that pay salaries by bank lines allocated to it), net pay is credited to that account INSTEAD of the bank, and the bank role is not consulted. That account must be an active, non-header liability with the payroll_liability subtype, not 2140/2150/2160/2175 and not one a loan uses: otherwise the run is refused with missing_net_pay_account (the account no longer exists), not_liability_net_pay_account, not_payroll_liability_net_pay_account, header_net_pay_account, net_pay_account_conflict, loan_net_pay_account, invalid_net_pay_setting (the stored setting cannot be read), net_pay_account_shared (another line of the journal, such as a cost-centre labour mapping, uses the same account) or inactive_target_account, and it never falls back to the bank. EMP201, UIF, SARS directive and loan payments still come from the bank. It also does not calculate or approve the run, does not pay anyone, and does not file an EMP201. ETI is booked net of labour cost and against PAYE payable, capped at the PAYE of the run: the labour debit and the PAYE credit both fall by min(ETI, PAYE), so the PAYE credit equals the EMP201 PAYE payable. ETI beyond PAYE is not booked and is reported as an eti_beyond_paye advisory. Reverse a posted payroll journal in the app; this tool will refuse a run that already has one rather than post a second.

tools.name: apply_receipt_to_invoice
tools.description: Apply a customer receipt to the invoices it settles: writes the allocation, raises each invoice's amount_paid and moves it to partially_paid or paid. This is what makes aged_debtors show what is OWED rather than everything ever invoiced. Name the cash with EXACTLY ONE of payment_id or bank_transaction_id. payment_id — an existing receipt whose journal has already posted (find them with list_unapplied_receipts): NO journal is posted, only the subledger moves. bank_transaction_id — an imported, unallocated bank line (find them with list_bank_transactions, and get suggested invoices from suggest_receipt_matches): ONE journal posts, DR Bank / CR Accounts Receivable, for the FULL amount of that line. Every invoice must belong to the same customer as the receipt, and no amount may exceed that invoice's outstanding balance. Applying less than the receipt is allowed and leaves a real unapplied remainder, which list_unapplied_receipts will keep reporting. Applying a receipt's remainder that a customer refund has already returned is refused (reverse the refund first, or apply only what is still on account). Does NOT cover: supplier payments (apply_payment_to_supplier_invoice), settlement against a loan or intercompany account without cash (settle_by_contra), credit notes (create_credit_note), or receipts that were posted straight to the control account by a journal with no customer payment record behind them — those are invisible to this tool. Run with dry_run first: it reports every balance that would move and writes nothing.

tools.name: reverse_journal_entry
tools.description: Reverse a POSTED journal entry by posting a contra entry that offsets it line for line. The original KEEPS status "posted" and is marked reversed in metadata, so the pair nets to zero in every report rather than the account swinging to the negative of the original. DATE: the contra is dated to the ORIGINAL entry date when that fiscal period is still open, and to TODAY when it is closed — a correction belongs in the period it corrects. Override with reversal_date, which must be a real YYYY-MM-DD day, must not fall before the entry being reversed, and must land in a fiscal period that EXISTS and is open. LOCKED VAT PERIODS: when the entry moves a VAT-return figure and the DEFAULT date falls inside a locked (filed) VAT period, the contra is dated forward to the first date outside every locked VAT period and inside an open fiscal period, and reversal_date_roll says so; a reversal_date you name inside a locked VAT period is refused. Refuses an entry that is a draft, already reversed, or has no lines. Does NOT cover: bank allocations (reverse_bank_allocation, or reverse_allocations for a date range) — reversing their journal directly would leave the bank transaction still marked allocated and pointing at an entry that has been undone. It also does not delete anything: both entries stay in the ledger, which is the point. Run with dry_run first: it reports the contra lines that would post and writes nothing.

tools.name: settle_by_contra
tools.description: Settle a customer invoice or a supplier bill against another GL account — a loan, intercompany or director's account — WITHOUT any cash moving. Use it when the debt was netted off rather than paid, which is otherwise only representable as a bank payment that never happened. subledger "ar" posts DR <contra account> / CR Accounts Receivable and reduces that invoice's outstanding balance. subledger "ap" posts DR Accounts Payable / CR <contra account> and reduces that bill's. Either way a payment document is created with payment_method "contra", so the settlement is afterwards distinguishable from a real bank movement. THE CONTRA ACCOUNT MUST BE A BALANCE-SHEET ACCOUNT — a loan, an intercompany or a director's account (type asset, liability or equity). Netting a debt against an EXPENSE or REVENUE account is a WRITE-OFF, not a contra, and is refused naming write_off (POST /api/accounting/write-offs), which has its own treatment. The side is decided from the account's type and subtype, never from its name or code. Also REFUSES a contra account that is a bank account (that is the phantom payment this exists to avoid), the subledger's own control account (it nets to nothing and settles the document against itself), a parent header account (the balance sheet excludes headers, so the posting would be invisible), a deactivated one, or one whose account_type and account_subtype are not a valid pairing (it cannot be classified, and this will not guess — fix it with update_gl_account). Also refuses an amount above the document's outstanding balance, and a cancelled or draft document. Partial settlement is allowed — the remainder stays outstanding. Does NOT cover: a real bank payment (apply_receipt_to_invoice / apply_payment_to_supplier_invoice), a credit note that reduces what is owed for a commercial reason (create_credit_note), or writing a debt off to bad debts, which is a policy decision rather than a settlement. Run with dry_run first: it reports the journal that would post and writes nothing.

tools.name: close_fiscal_period
tools.description: Close a fiscal period so nothing further can post into it. REFUSES on any failing readiness check and names every one of them with its reason — unreconciled banks, unposted draft journals, an AR or AP subledger that does not tie to its control account, an unbalanced trial balance, or a POSTED journal that belongs to no fiscal period at all — that last one is invisible to every period report while sitting in the ledger, so no close can honestly assert completeness over it. The app's own Close refuses on the same checks. A check that could not be COMPUTED also blocks — "the AP tie could not be checked" is exactly the state in which closing unattended is unsafe. Warnings (a period with no VAT return, uncleared opening-balance equity) do NOT block and come back in `warnings`. Also refuses a period that is locked, already closed, or has an open period before it. Run period_close_checklist or dry_run first: a dry run applies every one of these guards and writes nothing. Requires the write:post permission.

An already-open period is refused rather than reported as a change that did not happen. This weakens a control: everything dated inside the period becomes writable again, including by other agents. Reopen for a specific correction and close again. Requires write:post.
