tools.name: year_end_close
tools.description: Close a fiscal year: post a journal that zeroes every revenue and expense account into retained earnings, then LOCK every period in that year. Refuses while any period in the year is still open, and NAMES those periods so you know what to close first. Refuses when no retained-earnings account can be resolved. ALWAYS dry_run first. The dry run returns the whole journal — every line, the account codes, both totals and the net income — and writes nothing. This is not a routine posting: it moves a full year of trading into equity and then locks the periods, and locked periods cannot be reopened by any tool here. One production company has four unclosed years and R8.46m of retained earnings with no journal lines behind it, so equity is a computed residual; running this is how that stops being true, and it is worth reading the preview first. Requires the write:post permission.

tools.name: perform_bank_reconciliation
tools.description: Start a bank reconciliation for one account at a statement date and balance. It claims every unreconciled transaction of that account dated on or before the statement date: an ALLOCATED transaction is matched to its own allocation journal line at once (self_matched, confidence 1.0) when that line is a posted, unreversed bank-account line dated on or before the statement date; an unallocated (imported) transaction is auto-matched to an unclaimed posted GL line on the account. Reconciled and excluded transactions are never claimed. Auto-matching only applies matches it scores at 0.9 confidence or better; anything weaker is returned as a candidate for a person and is NOT applied. It does NOT create journals: a transaction with nothing in the GL to match stays unmatched — allocate it with allocate_bank_transaction and reconcile again. complete defaults to false. With complete: true the session is completed ONLY when the difference is exactly zero (recomputed from the ledger at completion) AND at least one transaction is matched (self-matches count) — an empty session balances trivially, because a reconciliation starts at the GL balance, and completing one proves nothing. Completion marks every matched and self-matched transaction reconciled. When either condition fails the call still SUCCEEDS, reports completed: false with the difference, and leaves the session in progress so the matches are not thrown away — cancel_bank_reconciliation releases it if you want to start over. Refuses if a reconciliation is already in progress on the account. dry_run reports the GL balance at the statement date, the difference against the statement balance you supplied, and how many transactions would be claimed and self-matched — and writes nothing. Requires the write:post permission.

auto_match.description: Run auto-matching after starting. Default true.

complete.description: Complete the reconciliation if it balances exactly. Default false. Completing marks every matched transaction reconciled and closes the session.

tools.name: lock_vat_period
tools.description: Records that a VAT period has been filed and stops it being changed. Stores the return that was filed — output tax, input tax, net VAT — together with the posted_through those figures were computed at, so that a later disagreement between the filed return and the ledger can be told apart from an arithmetic error. WHY YOU NEED IT: nothing else stops a journal being posted into a period that has already been filed. One live ledger accepts a 2022 posting made today, and the return submitted for 2022 no longer agrees with the ledger it came from, with nothing recording that it ever did. RUN dry_run FIRST. The dry run runs every guard the live call runs — the period must not run backwards, must not already be locked, and its 15% check is reported — and writes nothing. It REFUSES to lock a period whose rateCheck.ties is false unless you pass force:true, because a return that fails SARS's own check is not one to freeze; fix it or record explicitly that you are filing it as it stands. BOUNDS: the period must end on or before today, span at most 12 months, and not overlap another active lock. IDEMPOTENT BY THE PERIOD ITSELF: locking a period that is already locked returns the EXISTING lock and does not overwrite its figures, so a retry can never rewrite what was filed. ENFORCED: once locked, every posting that would move a VAT-return figure dated inside the period is refused (a journal with no VAT line still posts), and a reversal whose default date falls inside it is dated forward past the lock. LIMITS: there is no MCP unlock, deliberately — a lock an agent can lift with one call is not a control. An owner or admin unlocks it in the app, with a reason, and the unlocked lock is kept as history.

notes.description: Free text recorded with the lock, e.g. the eFiling reference.

force.description: Lock even though the 15% check fails. Records the decision; it does not make the return correct.

override_reason.description: Required to lock a period with blocking VAT exceptions outstanding (getVatExceptions). Owner/admin only — refused for any other role even with a reason. Recorded (never a silent bypass), and unrelated to force: force answers the 15% check, this answers whether the VAT is actually accounted for.

tools.name: take_audit_snapshot
tools.description: TAKE A SEALED AUDIT SNAPSHOT NOW at an accounting-date cutoff: the RAW LEDGER trial balance (a posted year-end closing journal is in it, so closed years show zero revenue and expense and the profit in retained earnings; the trial_balance report instead derives the close and skips that journal), every posted journal and line dated on or before it (each hashed), AR / AP ageing and control totals, and a check run, sealed with an HMAC. Append-only: it cannot be changed or deleted afterwards. Refused over the size cap (choose an earlier cutoff). dry_run: true runs the take's refusals (role, rate limit, signing key, busy, size cap) and returns how many posted lines it would freeze (snapshot.lines, against snapshot.maxLines), writing nothing; it cannot foresee the take running past its time budget (SNAPSHOT_TOO_SLOW). Owner or admin only; needs write:journals. Closing a period, locking a VAT period or closing a year takes one automatically. A snapshot holds the current values of records dated on or before its cutoff, as at taken_at — not the historical database state.

tools.name: set_bank_account_default_dimensions
tools.description: Set the default CC1 / CC2 / BU of a bank or paycard account (GL UUID or code, subtype bank). Card spend allocated to a cost account with no dimensions of its own takes these; a settlement never does. Each of cc1 / cc2 / bu: a code, UUID or alias to set, null to clear, omitted to keep. Posts nothing.

bank_account.description: GL account UUID or code of the bank / card account

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: set_supplier_default_dimensions
tools.description: Set the default CC1 / CC2 / BU of a supplier (migration 890). Every bill line of that supplier that names no CC1 or CC2 takes the default CC2 (and CC1); a line with no BU takes the default BU; a line's own dimensions always win, and posted bills are not touched. Each of cc1 / cc2 / bu: a code, UUID or alias to set, null to clear, omitted to keep. A default CC1 that contradicts the default CC2's FNO is refused. Posts nothing.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: split_allocate_bank_transaction
tools.description: Split ONE bank transaction across several lines — e.g. a paycard slip that is part fuel, part tolls, or one payment that settles two suppliers. Each line names exactly one of contra_account_id (a GL account, with its own vat_code and optional cc1 / cc2 / bu), supplier_id or customer_id. The line amounts are VAT-INCLUSIVE and must sum exactly to the transaction amount. POSTS one journal: a cost/revenue line per GL line (plus a VAT line where vat_code is standard), an AP/AR control line per supplier/customer line, and one bank line. A supplier/customer line gets its own payment, receipt or refund document on that journal, applied to the contact's oldest open documents unless auto_apply is "none" (then apply it with apply_payment_to_supplier_invoice / apply_receipt_to_invoice using the returned payment_id); it carries no VAT and no dimensions. Dimensions go on the GL cost/revenue lines only; a line on a control account may not carry them. When a GL line names none, the bank or card account's default dimensions apply. A cost-of-sales line with no project (cc2) is reported in dimension_warnings (or refused where the company requires a project). A vat_code the VAT guard would change (no supply possible, or input tax denied) is REFUSED. Use dry_run to preview. Undo with reverse_bank_allocation, which also cancels every document the split created.

transaction_id.description: Bank transaction UUID. Supply this OR bank_reference, not both.

bank_reference.description: The reference printed on the bank statement, matched exactly (after trimming) against either reference column on the transaction — the same value list_bank_transactions returns as bank_reference. Use it instead of transaction_id when working from a statement — no id lookup needed. Must resolve to exactly one transaction; if it does not, the tool lists the candidates.

bank_account_id.description: Optional: narrows a bank_reference lookup to one bank account.

contra_account_id.description: GL account UUID for this part of the transaction

supplier_id.description: Supplier UUID: this part pays (or is refunded by) that supplier

customer_id.description: Customer UUID: this part is a receipt from (or refund to) that customer

auto_apply.description: Supplier/customer lines only: "fifo" (default) applies to the oldest open documents; "none" leaves it on account.

cc1.description: Optional CC1 = FNO / client (code, UUID or alias). Usually omit it: a CC2 derives its FNO, and naming a CC1 that disagrees is refused.

cc2.description: Optional CC2 = project (code, UUID or alias, e.g. "Ben Farms"). Sets the FNO through its parent. A cost-of-sales line without one is reported in dimension_warnings.

bu.description: Optional business unit = function (code, UUID), e.g. "MAINT".

dry_run.description: Validate and preview; write nothing.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: tag_journal_lines
tools.description: Back-tag up to 500 POSTED journal lines with CC1 (FNO), CC2 (project) and/or BU — DIMENSIONS ONLY. Amounts, accounts, dates and VAT codes never change; any other field is refused. A CC2 derives its FNO; a conflicting cc1 is refused. Control-account lines (bank, AP, AR, VAT, payroll clearing) and settlement, receipt, transfer and VAT-payment journals are refused — the cost line carries the dimensions. Lines in a closed period are allowed and the batch is flagged a restatement. The bank transaction allocated to each journal touched MIRRORS that journal's CC1/CC2/BU when its dimension lines (every line but the bank leg that is not on a control account) agree on one set, NULLs included: a journal whose tags were all cleared clears the bank row (bank_rows_synced). Returns a batch_id; undo it (lines and bank rows) with reverse_dimension_tag_batch. Use dry_run first.

cc1.description: Code, UUID or alias to set; null clears it; omit to leave it unchanged.

cc2.description: Code, UUID or alias to set; null clears it; omit to leave it unchanged.

bu.description: Code, UUID or alias to set; null clears it; omit to leave it unchanged.

unallocated_reason.description: Why the line is tagged to the (unallocated) project.

reason.description: What this batch is, e.g. "FY26 back-tag from Lew ledger, Mar 2025".

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: reverse_dimension_tag_batch
tools.description: Undo a tag_journal_lines or sync_bank_dimensions batch: restore every line's and bank transaction's previous CC1 / CC2 / BU. Refused when a line or bank row was re-tagged by a later batch — reverse that one first. Changes dimensions only.

company_id.description: OPTIONAL guard, not a selector. The connector always acts on the company your token is bound to; passing this asserts which company you BELIEVE that is, and the call is refused if it differs. It can never redirect a write to another company. Resolve it once with list_companies.

tools.name: sync_bank_dimensions
tools.description: Make each ALLOCATED bank transaction carry the CC1 / CC2 / BU of its journal, so the Banking screen shows what the ledger carries (journal lines tagged before tag_journal_lines wrote through to the bank row). The bank row MIRRORS the journal: it takes the one set its POSTED journal's dimension lines (every line but the bank leg that is not on a control account: bank, AP, AR, VAT, payroll clearing) agree on, NULLs included — a journal tagged CC1-only BLANKS the row's CC2 and BU. A journal whose lines disagree (a split across projects, or one line tagged and another not) is left alone and shown as Split; a journal carrying no dimension at all (a supplier payment) leaves the row's own tags alone. date_from / date_to (bank transaction_date, inclusive) are required, and one run changes at most 2000 rows — narrow the window over that. DIMENSIONS ONLY — no amount, status or allocation moves. dry_run returns the count, a sample and `would_blank`: EVERY row where a value now held would become NULL, with the slots in `blanks` — read it before the live call. The live call records every row's old values under a batch_id; undo it with reverse_dimension_tag_batch (which needs write:post).
